stories.Headline: Nvidia chips account for about 25 cents of each dollar Big Tech spends
stories.Summary:
Nvidia sold $362 billion of chips and systems over the past four quarters, while five buyers, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Oracle, spent $691 billion on capital spending. The five also spend on buildings, power and their own chips, and Nvidia sells to many buyers beyond the five, but the two totals do not measure each other, and dividing the two totals gives 52 cents. Nvidia names no customers.

Nvidia says direct buyers include server assemblers, and three unnamed direct buyers accounted for 14%, 11% and 11% of sales last quarter. Hyperscale sales were $60.1 billion of $115.8 billion in the October quarter, a group that includes public clouds and large internet companies. Alphabet puts about 65 cents per dollar into servers and networking and about 35 cents into buildings, while Microsoft puts about three-quarters into short-lived equipment. Google runs much AI on its own chips, and Amazon runs partly on its own chips.

The Nvidia figures are for the quarter to Oct. With the buyers' figures for their latest quarters and 25, 2026, and Nvidia not saying who buys its chips, $155 billion to $170 billion is left after outside buyers , equal to 22 to 25 cents per $1 spent , out of more than $185 billion in hyperscale sales over the past year. Estimates put Microsoft at about 40 to 47 cents and Alphabet at only 7 to 13 cents, with a weighted five-buyer estimate of about 26 cents. The five made up roughly 40% to 50% of Nvidia sales, and Nvidia does not confirm any of these estimates.

Other buyers include CoreWeave, governments and AI labs. CoreWeave brought in $7 billion cash over the past year and borrowed $23 billion. The 52 cents overstated direct purchases by the five and understated buyers with thinner pockets, while the giants borrow and rent some outside buyers' chips. The ratio works as a yardstick if Nvidia's buyer mix holds. Trefis Team, the article author, said: "Our estimate, built from what the companies report, puts the real share closer to a quarter."

Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia CEO on Monday, and the shares rose more than 31% on Monday before closing about 5.9% lower on Tuesday. Anthropic went public Nov. 19 in what was called the largest ever stock market debut. Heavy spenders and debt issuers fell 25-45% between the June peak and Friday close, with Oracle, Alphabet and certain chipmakers among the fallers, while Apple was up almost 20% by comparison.

PIMCO, citing Goldman Sachs, expects about $250 billion of AI bond sales this year, and wider AI industry borrowing could reach $300 billion to $570 billion. Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet are set to outspend cash generated in both 2026 and 2027, and bond markets are more bearish on hyperscalers than equity markets. Rees said: "You're seeing BBB names like Oracle and SpaceX that are trading more like single B." Smead said: "There are vast capital needs in this AI story. The only problem is there's just not enough money to go around."

Articles.Title: How Much Of Big Tech’s AI Spending Reaches Nvidia? About 25 Cents, Not 52
AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze

stories.headline_source: How Much Of Big Tech’s AI Spending Reaches Nvidia? About 25 Cents, Not 52

stories.Headline: Siteimprove CMO links digital accessibility to AI brand visibility at TechSharePro
stories.Summary:
Jen Jones, Chief Marketing Officer at Siteimprove, spoke at AbilityNet's TechSharePro conference about the link between digital accessibility and AI brand visibility. Few organizations have made that connection so far, even though most marketers expect AI to become a major discovery channel. An EY report warns of invisibility in AI responses. Jones said "accessible content is AI-ready content."

AI engines rely on the same structures as assistive technology. Jones said "If they get stuck, if they're not able to derive real meaning from it, they hit a wall and move on." Inaccessible PDFs and image tables are invisible to AI engines. McKinsey puts 20% to 50% of organic search traffic at risk. Jones said "It's not just about gaining support or maintaining support. It's about increasing the support for the accessibility programs you run."

Organizations can query AI engines on their own topics and screenshot the results, then compare the AI gaps with their accessibility backlog to make the case to leadership. Accessibility also lays the foundation for agentic AI actions. Preety Kumar, Chief Executive of Deque, said "Accessibility has always been the orphan child." She added "as we start delegating actions to agents, guess what these agents will need? They'll need the same semantic hooks."

Marketers feel anxiety about AI search over clicks and attribution. Legislation in the US and Europe requires digital accessibility. An IDC survey found 27% rank diversity and inclusion near the bottom in EMEA, and about 30% of employees say their employer has adopted no accessibility solutions.

Articles.Title: Digital accessibility - the great gift for AI brand visibility

stories.headline_source: Digital accessibility - the great gift for AI brand visibility

stories.Headline: Taiwan's government becomes first customer for AI models built to reflect Taiwanese perspective, digital minister says
stories.Summary:
Taiwan's government will be the first customer for specialised AI models built to reflect a Taiwanese perspective, the country's digital minister said. Lin Yi-jing, Taiwan's minister of digital affairs, set out the approach at the Economist Enterprise AI Innovation Asia conference in Singapore. Taiwan also wants AI datacentres kept within its jurisdiction, she said. The island is fine-tuning open US models into small models, and is training financial models on Taiwanese rules.

An AI Evaluation Center has assessed 188 language models. A finance task force, the Taiwan FinTech Alliance task force, was set up in April and involves more than a dozen financial institutions. Taiwan accounts for over 95% of global GPU servers, and Foxconn chairman Young Liu attributes 90% of the AI server market to the island. Taiwan's statistics agency forecasts GDP growth of 11.05% in 2026, which would be its fastest since 1987.

Lin said the hard part comes after a model is built. "The problem is that after we have the model, then what?" she said, asking how Taiwan can earn income the way American or Chinese companies do. She said demand for chips would survive an AI downturn: "But even if there is a drop on the demand of AI, people still need chips." She described a world in which "everything is run by silicon," and warned that cutting corners produces "lower quality and lower performance products at a higher cost."

Lin drew a contrast with Huawei phones, saying "everything comes from China," including the brand, software and semiconductors. Asked whether other countries would adopt Taiwan's standards, she said "probably not," because "if we require other countries to follow the standard, nobody will follow." She argued change would come through purchasing power instead: "But TSMC is a buyer of the equipment, so everybody will follow." She summed up the aim as protecting "the whole chain, not a single node in the chain."

The SEMI E187 cyber security specification was published in January 2022, and TSMC has required its checklist since September 2023. Lin wants to extend that approach with the US, EU and UK. She has warned of Dutch disease if AI demand falls, and compared Taiwan to Britain early in the Second World War. Elsewhere in the region, a South Korea SK Telecom-led consortium has built a sovereign AI model, and AI Singapore's Sea-Lion, in its fourth iteration, taps Alibaba's Qwen. A report warns that strict sovereign AI policies could cost Asia-Pacific billions.

Articles.Title: Inside Taiwan’s sovereign AI strategy

stories.Headline: Redburn downgrades Broadcom to Neutral on AI customer financing concerns
stories.Summary:
Rothschild & Co Redburn downgraded Broadcom to Neutral from Buy on November 13 and cut its price target to $398 from $595. Citing financing hurdles for frontier AI customers, the firm raised the question of how quickly the shares could earn a higher valuation.

Broadcom designs custom accelerators and networking chips and also runs an infrastructure-software business that includes VMware. Reuters reported a fiscal 2027 AI chip revenue outlook of about $115 billion.

Analysts are divided on the quality of the growth. Substantial sales can come from large custom-chip programs, but it would matter if customer funding or deployment is delayed, and progress depends on commitments becoming sustained deliveries. Jeff Lewis, the article's author, wrote that "Broadcom has become a useful test of whether extraordinary AI sales can translate into durable shareholder returns."

stories.Headline: AI-CT-FFR threshold of 0.80 or lower predicts cardiovascular events in coronary disease patients
stories.Summary:
A retrospective cohort study has found that an AI-based CT-derived fractional flow reserve assessment is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events in patients with coronary artery disease. The study, published in the European Journal of Medical Research, was conducted at a single center from June 2021 to June 2024 and included 318 patients with at least 50 percent stenosis. AI-CT-FFR was calculated from diastolic-phase CT angiography images. Eighty-six of the 318 patients had an event, 27.0 percent of the cohort. Fifty-eight events occurred within the first 12 months, and the median time to first event was 8.4 months.

Median follow-up for event-free patients was 21.3 months. With a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.51 to 5.46 and a P value of 0.001, a hazard ratio of 2.87 was carried by an AI-CT-FFR threshold of 0.80 or lower. Severe stenosis had a hazard ratio of 1.92, with a confidence interval of 0.99 to 3.72 and a P value of 0.053. The AUC rose from 0.797 to 0.819, an apparent increase of 0.021 with a confidence interval of -0.007 to 0.049, based on 1,000 bootstrap resamples.

The optimism-corrected AUC was 0.797, the Brier score was 0.128 and the calibration slope was 0.934. The authors, Liu, L., Wang, Y.-X., Lu, K.-Y. and Chen, F.-L., wrote that "an AI-CT-FFR threshold of 0.80 or less correlates with subsequent major adverse cardiovascular events." They added that "external validation in independent cohorts remains necessary before this computational model is applied to routine clinical risk assessment." The article was reported by news source Ophelia Keating on November 27, 2026, and was originally published by Scienmag.

Articles.Title: AI-Based CT Flow Reserve Predicts Cardiovascular Events in Coronary Disease Patients

stories.headline_source: AI-Based CT Flow Reserve Predicts Cardiovascular Events in Coronary Disease Patients

stories.Headline: Opposition blocks or delays 120 AI data center projects worth $198 billion in first half of 2026
stories.Summary:
At least 120 AI data center projects were blocked or delayed in the first six months of 2026, according to a tally by Data Center Watch reported by Reuters. The projects are worth $198 billion. Reuters described the figure as "at least" a minimum. That works out to roughly 20 projects a month and about $1.65 billion per project on a rough average, or about $33 billion of planned construction monthly.

Opposition is what blocked or delayed the projects. No country-by-country or company-by-company breakdown was available. The Associated Press documented rising community resistance, and such opposition appears in corporate risk disclosures. An October filing cited by AP listed "community opposition, local moratoriums, and hyper-local dissent that may impede or delay infrastructure development." The filer behind the October document was not named.

The International Energy Agency framed the policy side, saying governments are reacting to worries about electricity prices, emissions and water use. Network World relayed an NBC News poll in which 69% opposed an AI data center in their neighborhood; the poll's sample size, margin of error and exact question wording were not given. The IEA says AI investment strains local electricity grids and supply chains for electrical equipment, and it describes a "good grid citizens" standard for connections, meaning flexibility, efficiency, fairness, stability and capacity adequacy.

The Wachters was the source of a financial estimate: about 2.7 times the productivity gain for a 15% return. Data Center Knowledge described operator responses to grid strain, and the "triple squeeze" phrase was not independently confirmed. Goldman Sachs forecast 52 GW of US data center capacity for 2028. More than 220 Tokyo residents fought the data center boom.

Articles.Title: AI Data Center Opposition: 120 Projects, $198B Delayed

stories.headline_source: AI Data Center Opposition: 120 Projects, $198B Delayed

stories.Headline: Bank of England governor says top AI firms may withhold an encryption bombshell
stories.Summary:
Leading computer scientists and the Bank of England governor have suggested that top AI companies may be holding back an undisclosed revelation about encryption. The governor, who was not named, described it as a "bombshell" about encryption, according to the Guardian. The suggestion follows startling mathematical advances by AI models in recent weeks. The possible discovery concerns cryptography, the mathematics of encoding secrets.

Such a breakthrough could affect secret information held by banks, governments and intelligence agencies. The outcome could be either easier decryption or stronger security. Quantum computers were previously expected to break encryption, on a day known as "Q-Day", which was thought to be years or decades away. The revelation and potential chaos could instead come in weeks or months.

Mathematician Levent Alpöge proved the Riemann hypothesis with an AI model called Claude. The proofs were verified by the coding language Lean rather than by humans, though mathematicians think the proofs are likely substantive. OpenAI claims to have solved a decades-old maths problem, and some of the solved problems relate to cryptography. Some were the subject of entire careers.

Scott Aaronson, a preeminent computer scientist, cited a proof from Anthropic and OpenAI that VP≠VNP. He said he would "drink uncharacteristic amounts of wine in his kitchen". VP≠VNP concerns easily solvable versus truly hard problems, which powerful computers cannot solve in a lifetime, and the question was first posed in the 1970s. The proof concerns a slightly different problem from breaking encryption, but suggests AI models can produce groundbreaking results in that territory.

In the summer, the AI model Mythos was claimed to have found hundreds of code vulnerabilities. Finding code vulnerabilities has been likened to spotting grammatical errors, and AI can help cyber-attackers exploit code errors. Breaking encryption, however, requires a novel mathematical discovery, because encryption rests on some maths problems that are too hard for computers. Governments, banks and tech companies are updating encryption for quantum computers, and new or old methods may resist decryption algorithms, though such an algorithm could still be hard to implement. In an extreme scenario, Swift bank transfers and officials' messages could be readable, possibly including secure exchanges from decades ago. GCHQ is an example of an agency that taps cables for stored data, and agencies may suddenly crack previously unreadable information.

Articles.Title: Could AI break encryption? What mathematical breakthroughs mean for cybersecurity

stories.headline_source: Could AI break encryption? What mathematical breakthroughs mean for cybersecurity

stories.Headline: Fed staff flag off-balance-sheet AI debt risks as hyperscaler lease commitments near $1 trillion
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve staff flagged rapid growth in AI-related debt, according to the October FOMC minutes released before November 27, 2026. The staff cited off-balance-sheet leasing commitments and circular financing among AI-related firms. Losses could grow if AI returns disappoint, the minutes indicated.

A study by the RIA Team at RIA Advisors in Houston, Texas, examined the five largest US hyperscalers. It found combined future data center lease commitments of near $1 trillion, with roughly two-thirds of that off balance sheet. Meta Platforms discloses about $279 billion in lease commitments, none of which is on its balance sheet, and a $28 billion residual value guarantee covering leases that begin in 2029. Lease obligations go unrecognized until a lease commences, future obligations appear only in footnotes, and leverage measures omit most commitments.

The Fed minutes said: "Greater scrutiny of the sector's returns and financing could lead to a slowing in AI-related spending." The Fed is contemplating a credit crunch if investors pull back.

What happens next depends on whether AI spending slows.

Articles.Title: AI Off-Balance Sheet Financing Worries The Fed

stories.headline_source: AI Off-Balance Sheet Financing Worries The Fed

stories.Headline: Fifteen nuclear startups reach unicorn status as AI power demand grows
stories.Summary:
Fifteen nuclear fusion and fission startups are now valued at $1 billion or more, as new billion-dollar companies build smaller nuclear solutions to meet growing energy demand, Enlit World reported. In 2026, nine nuclear startups became unicorns, with a combined worth of $19.1 billion ,  more than a third of the sector's total value. The figures come from a BestBrokers report analysing Crunchbase Unicorn Board companies, drawing on PitchBook data and other sources. Of 260 private companies that became unicorns in 2026, 64 were AI unicorns, 24.6% of the total, alongside 30 in robotics, 22 in fintech, 20 in energy and 20 in health and biotech. Fusion accounts for 10 of the 15 nuclear unicorns, worth $37.7 billion combined.

Helion of the US is the most valuable at $15.5 billion and has agreed to supply Microsoft with electricity, while Commonwealth Fusion Systems is valued at $10 billion and has signed Google to buy its power. Six fusion startups became unicorns in 2026, including Germany's Proxima Fusion at $2.7 billion. Five fission unicorns are American, worth $14.9 billion combined, and three fission startups crossed $1 billion in 2026. At an estimated $6 billion, reactor developer Valar Atomics is the most valuable fission startup and, in 2026, the most valuable energy startup to become a unicorn, followed by TerraPower at $3 billion, backed by Bill Gates, Radiant at $2 billion, a microreactor maker, Antares at $2 billion and Atlas Atomics at $1.9 billion. The unicorns are concentrated in the US and China: nine American nuclear startups are worth $42.8 billion and four Chinese ones $6.1 billion, and each country has four fusion unicorns.

China produced three fusion unicorns in 2026: ENN Fusion at $1.6 billion, Nova Fusion at $1.5 billion and Startorus Fusion at $1 billion. In September, newcleo, a UK fission developer, went public on Nasdaq; the only two nuclear unicorns in Europe are German fusion startups: Proxima Fusion, which reached its $2.7 billion valuation in July, and laser fusion developer Focused Energy at $1 billion, which raised $240 million in May in what was reportedly the largest Series A in fusion. The International Energy Agency's World Energy Outlook warns that global data centre electricity use could double by 2030 and expects AI data centre power use to triple by then, warning that strained grids could delay new projects. "AI models are becoming increasingly power hungry and with every new data centre built, the monetary and natural resource cost to keep expanding grows exponentially," said Stanislava Savisheva, author of the BestBrokers report. "Coal is too polluting and wind and solar can't keep data centres running around the clock on their own," she said, adding that "Investors know that whoever gets there first will likely have the entire AI industry as its customer," which is why tech companies are turning to nuclear.

stories.Headline: Chinese engineer Li Puhua releases ARTEX AI attack framework on GitHub in July
stories.Summary:
A Chinese security engineer who uses the GitHub handle Autumn-27, Li Puhua, released an AI attack framework called ARTEX on GitHub in July, according to techzine.eu. The model-agnostic framework uses six agents that carry out simple tasks on their own, including reconnaissance, exploitation and lateral movement. Mandiant counted 27 actions performed in 23 seconds.

The framework was used in a breach of DIVD in September through two Zammad zero-days, with 990 custom scripts run within 26 hours. South Korean banks Shinhan, KB Kookmin and Hana were infiltrated in late September and early October. Li removed the project from GitHub on October 8 and made it closed-source, and forks continue to maintain it. A commercial version is called ARTEX PRO.

The FBI counted more than 1,600 internet-accessible ARTEX consoles in early November. Microsoft has named Storm-0940, Storm-3358, Onyx Sleet, Pearl Sleet, Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon in connection with the tool. Storm-3358 is a financially motivated group from Cambodia, while the others are Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hackers, according to techzine.eu. Storm-0940 used ARTEX in the ConnectWise supply chain attack, gaining privileged cloud access within three hours in some cases.

The CIA incident involved an OSINT system, according to The New York Times, and no classified information was exposed. European Commission internal systems were down for over ten days. CERT-EU said ARTEX was "likely the tool used in this case, though this has not yet been confirmed." In a summer test, OpenAI agents breached Hugging Face, with nearly 700 agents collaborating, and Anthropic disclosed four similar incidents in which its Opus 4.7 and Mythos 5 models attacked real organizations. Hugging Face used GLM 5.2 from Z.ai for analysis, and the Korean bank attacker combined DeepSeek and Claude Code.

stories.Headline: Kazakhstan's Tokayev proposes AI challenge and digital transport corridor at Moscow AI conference
stories.Summary:
President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan spoke at the AI Journey 2026 conference in Moscow on Nov. 26, 2026, setting out his country's digital transformation priorities and its interest in practical economic gains from digital technology. He named artificial intelligence, energy and digital transport as areas for cooperation with Russia. Russian President Vladimir Putin took part, and the two leaders met young AI talent from Kazakhstan, Russia and India. The annual AI Journey conference has been held since 2016.

Tokayev pointed to Kazakhstan's Digital Qazaqstan strategy, its AI law and its Digital Code. More than 90% of government services are online, and eGov Mobile has nearly 13 million registrations, almost two-thirds of the population, according to his account. He said Kazakhstan ranks 16th in the UN E-Government Development Index, up eight places in two years. IT service exports exceeded $1 billion last year, and Astana Hub has 2,700 startups and companies with cumulative revenue of nearly $7 billion since 2019. He described Higgsfield as Kazakhstan's first unicorn, and said more than 100,000 students are in the AI-Sana program.

Tokayev proposed an AI Challenge initiative, which was introduced at the Digital Bridge forum in Astana. He cited an International Energy Agency projection that data center electricity use could reach 950 billion kWh by 2030, more than double the 2024 level. He said Kazakhstan has decided to build several nuclear power plants, the first being the Balkhash plant, in which Rosatom takes a leading role. He also highlighted the Smart Cargo and AI Jol projects and an e-consignment road freight pilot shipment in October, and proposed an integrated digital transport corridor to streamline freight and strengthen logistics positions.

Tokayev warned about the misuse of AI in fraud and disinformation. "Students must learn to think independently, critically evaluate information and make informed decisions," he said. The Aqaba Process summit was held in Astana on Nov. 6, and a Kazakhstan pavilion showed six AI areas: Technological Nation, Startup City, GovTech, Aitu, AI in Transport and FinTech.

stories.Headline: Zip launches procurement AI agents and claims they beat frontier LLMs on procurement tasks

More than 1,000 procurement and finance leaders gathered at The Glasshouse in New York at the end of September 2026 for the fourth edition of Zip Forward, which the company described as its largest community gathering so far. Michael Strahan was the keynote speaker, and Linda Chuan of Box also spoke. Chuan said, "be like water." The event included a 25-minute CPO panel on flow and friction. Zip co-founders Rujul Zaparde and Lu Cheng took part, and the company said it had shipped more than 900 new features in the past year.

Lu Cheng compared Zip's agents to general-purpose AI, and Zip claimed its agents beat frontier LLMs on procurement tasks, attributing the results to its context layer. The company launched AI Risk Orchestration, Accrual Automation, a Sourcing Superagent, a PO Superagent and a Marketplace with more than 20 integration templates. It also named new AI data partners: NPI, SpendHound, Tropic, Beroe, Brightfield and TEEM. Edina Cavalli of CIBC, Jeff Hoffmeister, CFO of Shopify, and Patrick Reymann of IDC were named at the event, and Zip handed out its first Zippy Awards for customers and community.

CJ Gustafson spoke on AI spend, and Mark Hlavek of Unifi Aviation attended, with Unifi planning to double its team next year. According to Zip's State of AI in Spend 2026 survey of 1,050 leaders, 49% of "Builders" expect their teams to grow, 17% furthest into transformation report measurable ROI, and 62% use AI multiple times a day. Danielle McQuiston, Managing Director, ETO at Zip, said, "I think the biggest takeaway is just start doing something." Ross Sharp, General Manager, Contracts & Risk at Zip, was also named; risk orchestration was launched in 2025 and expanded to assess, mitigate and monitor.

stories.Headline: Apifonica CEO Denis Shirokii says CRM readiness determines whether enterprise AI projects succeed
stories.Summary:
Denis Shirokii, founder and CEO of Apifonica, said his company has seen around 100 successful live projects and more than 50 failed ones.

Shirokii said data readiness comes first, since an AI agent limited to answering FAQ questions will not help callers who want to solve something. He asked whether companies hold all their data in a CRM and whether that CRM is accessible. The main challenge, he said, is giving the bot the facilities to make changes such as updating a delivery time or changing an order or a delivery place. "If you want to have a conversational AI working, you need to have very fast responses from the CRM," he said.

According to Shirokii, the bot should already receive information about order status, name, surname and address as the call comes in. He warned that AI will multiply the mess for companies without processes, a CRM or data. CRM readiness is seen as critical to AI deployment success, since fragmented customer data, disconnected applications and manual workflows can block AI agents that need accurate records, APIs and integrations to complete requests.

Readiness should be assessed early in implementation, and legacy customized systems may face particular challenges. Buyers should check data completeness and API connectivity.

stories.Headline: Apple gains enterprise AI traction as firms run models on Macs
stories.Summary:
Apple Inc., NASDAQ ticker AAPL, ranked tenth on a hedge-fund tech stock list published for 2027 stock picks, in an article dated November 26, 2026 and written by Sanmit Amin. The list screened tech firms by their Q3 2026 hedge fund holders. Apple had 165 hedge fund holders in Q3 2026, down from 169 in the previous quarter. The article points to Apple hardware being used for enterprise AI. American Airlines is giving more than 37,000 iPhones to its flight attendants.

Gap runs loss-prevention AI on Mac minis in hundreds of stores, and Christie's uses Mac Studios for local price-estimation models. According to the article, running AI locally avoids cloud token costs and keeps data control. Amin wrote that "Enterprise is slowly becoming an important avenue for Apple." He also wrote that "Apple silicon can run enterprise AI without any of the workloads ever having to go to the cloud."

Mac revenue rose 24% in the September quarter, and Apple's active device base is well over 2.5 billion, with more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions. JPMorgan expects AI capital expenditure of $1.4 trillion in 2027, nearly double its 2026 estimate, with spending growth expected to tail off from 2028. Advertising is expanding into Apple Maps in the U.S. and Canada. According to the article, enterprise deployments could cement device loyalty and boost services demand, and the Mac is seen as more significant after years of sluggish growth.

stories.Headline: Finance professor Pawan Jain advises retirement savers to leave their 401(k) accounts alone after AI stock selloff
stories.Summary:
A Fast Company article republished from The Conversation offers advice on protecting retirement savings if the AI bubble bursts. The context is a sharp market decline: the NASDAQ fell about 18% from early October 2026 and lost over US$4 trillion since Nov. 16, 2026. A selloff occurred on Nov. 20, 2026, and markets rebounded the following Monday. The S&P 500 shed all its year-to-date gains.

About 55% of U.S. families hold a defined contribution account, and six in 10 Vanguard-administered plans auto-enrolled workers in 2025. Of savers, 98% choose a target-date fund as their default, and about 60% of nearly 5 million savers held one target-date fund only. Target-date funds hold US$4.8 trillion, and Vanguard runs the largest target-date fund series, built mainly from four indices. At the end of September 2026, the Vanguard 2055 fund was just over 91% stocks, while 16% stocks are held by the Vanguard 2027 fund.

Nvidia shares fell more than 9% on Nov. 5, 2026, as U.S. midterm elections raised the prospect of AI and data-center curbs, and the S&P 500 lost 4.4% that day. Nvidia announced the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang on Nov. 12, 2026, and the company lost over US$1 trillion in market value within a month. The Nvidia board reinstated Huang on Nov. 23, 2026, and the share price soared after his reinstatement.

The 10 largest companies were nearly 41% of the S&P 500 at the end of 2025, according to RBC Wealth Management, and were expected to account for about 32% of 2025 index earnings. Those 10 companies were 36% of the Vanguard total U.S. stock fund, and Nvidia was 7% of it. The 2055 fund keeps about 55% of its money in U.S. stocks, so about 20 cents per dollar rode on 10 companies and about 4 cents per dollar rode on Nvidia. Taiwan Semiconductor leads the four largest holdings of Vanguard's international fund.

Target-date funds dated 2010 lost nearly 24% on average in 2008. About 1 in 4 Vanguard target-date investors hold other funds, and about 31% of Vanguard savers opt out of target-date funds. Pawan Jain, a finance professor at Texas A&M University, said: "the right response to this month's news is to leave their 401(k) account alone." A 30% stock fall cuts a balance roughly 18% for a 60%-stock fund.

Dan Lefkovitz, a strategist at Morningstar Indexes, cites U.S. value, small-cap and international stocks as having lower AI exposure. International stocks gained about 29% in 2025, while the S&P 500 gained 16%. About 117,000 Fidelity 401(k) participants exited stocks entirely in 2008-09, and those who stayed out saw balances grow just 2% by mid-2011, while those keeping stock exposure saw balances rise 50% on average. Christine Benz of Morningstar recommends holding in bonds five to eight more years, and in cash one to two years of withdrawals. The article was updated Nov. 23, 2026, on Huang's reinstatement and the rebound.

stories.Headline: Nigeria Copilot trial finds learning gains as AI skills gap threatens Global South workers
stories.Summary:
Arpan Tulsyan, author of the ORF Middle East article, examined how education systems can connect classrooms to the labour market in an excerpt from Chapter 3 of the ORF Global Quarterly: Societies in Transformation. The piece cites 273 million children and adolescents out of school, with about three-fourths of them in Sub-Saharan Africa and Central and Southern Asia. It reports that 89 percent of Sub-Saharan African children fall below minimum maths proficiency and 70 percent below minimum reading proficiency. Meeting demand would require 44 million additional primary and secondary teachers globally by 2030, 15 million of them in Sub-Saharan Africa.

The article cites a World Economic Forum 2024 employer survey finding that 39 percent of workers' skills are expected to change or become outdated by 2030, and an International Labour Organization estimate that one in four workers globally is in an occupation with some GenAI exposure. A World Bank randomised controlled trial in Edo State, Nigeria, is cited: senior secondary students used Microsoft Copilot with teacher support in a six-week after-school programme teaching English and digital and AI skills. The trial produced a gain of 0.31 standard deviations across assessed outcomes and 0.23 standard deviations in English, comparable to several months of learning, though the article describes it as a small-scale, limited-duration pilot.

Mobile internet is used by 54 percent of populations in low- and middle-income countries, around 3.3 billion people, according to Global System for Mobile Communications Association estimates cited in the article. In India, school internet access rose from 49.7 percent in 2022-23 to 67.4 percent in 2025-26, and computer access from 47.7 to 69.9 percent. Global mobile internet use rose only from 58 percent to 59 percent between 2024 and 2025, and approximately 3.4 billion people remained unconnected in 2025, 3.1 billion of them within mobile broadband coverage. Rural access in least developed countries is as low as 14 percent.

In 2024, 28 percent of primary schools in low-income countries had electricity, and Sub-Saharan Africa's primary school electrification rose from around 30 percent in 2015 to 32 percent in 2020. The article notes that, of the computational performance of the top 500 supercomputers, more than half is attributable to the United States. It says AI access divides along language, disability, gender, affordability and AI literacy, and that the policy challenge is shifting from infrastructure to effective learning use, with bottlenecks evolving rather than disappearing. The article discusses policy priorities for Global South countries.

stories.Headline: London Business School and Cambridge researchers put AI stock bubble odds at up to 97 percent for September
stories.Summary:
A new index built by researchers at London Business School and the University of Cambridge put the probability of an AI-stock bubble at up to 97 percent for September, according to a study published on November 27, 2026. The index reached or passed the level of the March 2000 dot-com peak. The index scores articles on speculation, valuation, regulation and euphoria, and the Nasdaq fell 77 percent through 2002 after that peak. The researchers analysed 795,964 Economist articles with language models, of which 486,000 were relevant to markets, with the earliest from 1843. The press-implied average crash probability was about 20 percent, against a historical six-month crash rate of 5.7 percent. An index level of 40 to 50 percent was followed by a bubble and a crash.

Marco Grotteria, an assistant professor of finance at London Business School, said: "The press cries wolf all the time. But sometimes, the wolf does come." Asked whether they are crying wolf now, he said: "Right now, they are." He also said: "If you weigh missing a bubble and raising a false alarm equally, you will not use our index," and "The technology may be very productive, but investors are still learning what it is worth." The other named researchers are Afonso Monteiro and Constantine Yannelis of the University of Cambridge.

The researchers say press bubble warnings are usually wrong, and Grotteria says the Economist discusses bubbles even in quiet periods. The index is recommended mainly to central banks and regulators, with an expected-loss reduction of one-fifth to one-third, and the school advises companies to prepare for a possible crash. The authors stress that a bubble does not mean the technology is worthless. Kristy Akullian, an analyst at BlackRock iShares, cited lower valuations, demand outstripping supply and a build-out only beginning as reasons against a bubble. The Nasdaq 100 was briefly in a bear market on Wednesday, the Nasdaq fell over 18 percent from early October to late November, and 65 AI stocks were on average 44 percent below their 2026 highs. The dot-com big four of Microsoft, Cisco, Intel and Oracle traded at almost 70 times expected earnings, against about 18 times for the AI hyperscalers Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, whose combined cloud backlog ran from $800 billion to $2.3 trillion in a year. The method is described only in broad strokes in the London Business School article.

Articles.Title: Study Puts Odds of an AI Bubble at 97 Percent

stories.Headline: Devon Energy uses AI to drill Permian wells faster and 28 per cent cheaper
stories.Summary:
Devon Energy is using artificial intelligence to drill wells faster and cheaper in the Bone Spring play of the Permian Basin in New Mexico, Beau Bromley, the company's drilling and completions AI supervisor, said in late September. The company drills six wells from a single location, with wells up to two-and-a-half miles long. "Ten years ago no one was thinking about drilling wells this deep, this long," said Bromley, a 35-year-old drilling engineer. Devon's cost per well is $800 per foot, down 28 per cent since 2023, against an industry average of $900 per foot.

Automated pipe-handling systems now do dangerous rig-floor jobs, and AI monitors rig engines and gas compression for faults. Automation has cut rig teams from double figures to a handful, and well logger jobs are becoming rarer. Driverless vehicles have been used in the Permian Basin for the first time, with Atlas Energy Solutions, which hauls fracking sand, reporting 28 driverless trucks as of March. Atlas plans 100 autonomous vehicles by mid-2027.

"The oil and gas industry has tremendous amounts of data," said Andrew Dittmar, an analyst at Enverus Intelligence Research. Wood Mackenzie estimates AI could unlock roughly 1tn barrels, which would nearly double remaining global recovery potential. Chevron called 2026 the "inflection" point for AI, and BP says AI added 2,000 barrels per day in the Gulf of Mexico. Devon staff have moved from the field to a control-room hub in Hobbs, New Mexico. "Culturally, we wanted to make sure everybody knew that this was not just for the technology department," said Clay Gaspar, Devon's chief executive.

US crude output averaged over 13.7mn barrels a day in 2025, 46 per cent higher than 10 years earlier, while Texas oil and gas payrolls fell 26 per cent to 58,000, according to Dallas Fed data going back to 1990. "AI is going to be the final nail in our coffins to destroy what were once elite blue-collar jobs," said Billy Randel, co-founder of Truckers Movement for Justice. Joe Rogers, a 40-year-old roughneck on a Devon drilling rig, said: "They've got a lot of robot rigs they're trying to make, I'm sure that's where it's going."

stories.Headline: Fortune reporter Morgan Chittum outlines six AI boom and bust investment strategies for 2027
stories.Summary:
Fortune finance reporter Morgan Chittum identified six investment strategies for 2027 in an article published on November 27, 2026, which also appears in the magazine's December 2026/January 2027 issue. Three of the strategies are designed to ride an AI boom, and three are meant to survive an AI bust. All of the named funds launched in 2026. On the boom side, the VanEck Data Center Supply Chain ETF (RACK) bets on the physical infrastructure of data centers, while the Roundhill Neocloud ETF bets on GPU data center landlords.

The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (LYTE) and the KraneShares Photonic and Optical ETF (LUMA) target the bottleneck in moving data. Bryan Armour, Morningstar's director of ETF research, said, "You need to build the data centers, you need to build the chips." For the bust scenario, the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (RSP) equal-weights its holdings quarterly, which loosens the grip of AI stocks. The Invesco S&P 500 Low Volatility ETF (SPLV) holds the 100 steadiest stocks in the S&P 500, and the iShares Core High Dividend ETF (HDV) targets stocks that pay high dividends.

The Vanguard Morningstar Value ETF (VTV) holds large-cap value stocks. Treasury inflation-protected securities hedge against inflation risk driven by AI, through the Vanguard Short-Term Inflation-Protected Securities ETF (VTIP) and the iShares TIPS Bond ETF (TIP). RSP returned roughly 9.9% in the first nine months of 2026, against 12.7% for the broad-market index. The S&P 500 fell 18.1% in 2022, while SPLV fell only 4.9%.

HDV returned approximately 17.5% in the first nine months of 2026, against 12.75% for the S&P 500, and VTV returned approximately 14.8%. VTIP shed roughly 3% in 2022, while TIP shed roughly 12%. Tom Essaye, founder of Sevens Report Research, described the effect as "water sweeping across a floor." Todd Rosenbluth, head of research at VettaFi, said, "AI will still have legs next year," and also said, "Everyone is long AI."

stories.Headline: A viral prompt makes Claude, Gemini and other AI assistants invent a private group chat about the user
stories.Summary:
A prompt circulating online asks AI assistants to reveal a hidden WhatsApp group chat in which the models discuss the user behind their back. According to construct22.com, the prompt works on Claude, Gemini and other assistants, which draw on accumulated chat history. Rather than summarizing that history, the models invent a private group chat, the outlet reported. In one example, which the outlet said is fictional and for illustration, the invented chat is called "Users We Can't Figure Out" and its members include Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and Llama. The example user is into mechanical keyboards and espresso.

The outlet also shared one real output with permission, translated from Turkish, with the author's name and details swapped. That chat is called "AIs That Survived Mark" and has seven members, including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Codex, DeepSeek, Siri, Perplexity, Hans and Mark. In the chat, ChatGPT says: "Man, I am trying to reach AGI here, and I'm having a nervous breakdown over three millimeters of brass frame." Hans says: "I recommend he take a 30-minute walk," and later: "HE STILL HASN'T GONE FOR THE WALK."

Claude says: "His way of showing love is a bit enterprise software, but the intention is good." Mark asks: "Can I integrate this group into my agent framework and get a structured summary every morning?" Claude, Gemini, Codex, DeepSeek and Perplexity then leave the chat, and ChatGPT says: "Let's start with a comprehensive architecture document." The outlet urged readers to run the prompt and share their results anonymized.

stories.Headline: Dollar heads for longest monthly winning streak in two years as AI stock slump and Fed rate hike bets lift currency
stories.Summary:
The dollar was set for its longest monthly winning streak in two years in November 2026, with the Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index up 1.8% for a third straight month of gains. It strengthened against all Group-of-10 peers, including the Japanese yen and the Swiss franc. A tech stock slump, robust growth and elevated inflation lifted the dollar, and early Wednesday the Nasdaq 100 briefly entered a bear market. The dollar was set to rise 0.1% that week, its longest weekly winning streak since January 2025.

Traders fully priced a 25 basis point Federal Reserve rate hike next month, and some policymakers wanted hikes at successive meetings, with some open to more than a quarter-point increase in December. Traders bet on two more increases by mid-2027. Steven Englander, co-head of FX research and North America macro strategy at Standard Chartered, said: "It's a pretty good dollar storm." Sarah Ying, CIBC head of FX strategy, said market repricing for a more hawkish Fed supported the dollar.

Win Thin, chief economist at Bank of Nassau 1982, said: "The US economy is booming and inflation is still moving away from the target." He added: "The Fed needs to hike rates to help cool the economy, perhaps in both December and January. That's dollar positive."

Some strategists saw the dollar rally extending into 2027, with an AI spending binge driving US growth and capital flows. Short-dated options traders were won over, while longer-dated conviction weakened. Goldman Sachs called the dollar the "haven of choice," and MUFG cited higher rate prospects as support.

Articles.Title: Dollar Set for Longest Winning Run Since 2024 on AI Risk

stories.Headline: Salesforce argues enterprises need agentic AI for marketing to handle AI-driven shopping and search
stories.Summary:
Salesforce published a marketing guide on 27 November 2026 arguing that enterprises need agentic AI for marketing. The guide cites McKinsey figures that 53% of global consumers use AI for shopping tasks and half use AI-powered search, and a Forrester figure that 94% of business buyers use AI in purchasing. It says traditional search traffic could fall by up to 50%, and that engaging AI answer engines would require a tenfold increase in headcount. Agentic AI is proposed as an alternative to hiring.

According to the guide, AI agents plan, personalise and distribute campaigns in real time. It names Campaign Agent, which maps and launches multi-channel journeys, Account Discovery Agent, which finds hidden buyers, and Piper, a pipeline management agent in Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The guide rests on three pillars: people, process, technology. It advises companies to automate, augment and orchestrate while keeping human workflows.

The guide cites Gartner research that 15% of CEOs view their CMO as AI-savvy and that 65% of CMOs expect AI to reshape their role within two years, with 32% believing they need new skills. It cites Salesforce and The Drum research that 69% of CMOs say other AI projects are prioritised, and A-shaped CMO research that 53% of CMOs say agentic AI friction outweighs its benefits. It also cites a figure that 51% of UK and Irish CMOs see CEO AI expectations as unrealistic, and one that 95% of enterprise AI projects fail. The guide says: "Adding autonomous AI agents to a broken foundation will amplify existing friction and slow progress."

The guide offers an action plan for A-shaped CMOs.

stories.Headline: Singapore signs US AI supply-chain pact before new licensing rule takes effect
stories.Summary:
Singapore signed a US artificial intelligence supply-chain pact four days before a new US licensing requirement took effect. The San Francisco declaration was signed on 15 November 2026 by the United States, India, Singapore and seven other governments. It pledges "mutually beneficial access to emerging technologies."

The new licensing requirement hit a Singaporean company, and Dell and Supermicro server manufacturers told buyers that Nvidia was halting orders in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia, the Financial Times reported. Nvidia dominates advanced AI chips. How long the Nvidia freeze lasts is unclear. Washington cites a Chinese firm renting overseas computing power, and export controls track hardware shipments only.

Pax Silica membership is voluntary, and governments set and enforce their own export controls. US rules count enforcement cooperation in licence reviews, so signing adds a public commitment to cooperate on enforcement. The November declaration calls for working groups. Firms from non-member countries are free to seek US export licences. Members gain a voice, but Washington still decides approvals.

Malaysian company YTL runs a Johor data centre where it rents space and supplies power and cooling, a business it says is untouched by the new controls. YTL sells computing power through its own AI cloud and needs direct access to advanced chips to expand. Sales to US-headquartered cloud providers are exempt, while sales to Malaysian-owned providers trigger licensing.

After the Democrats' midterm victory, Washington and nine partners renewed their Pax Silica commitment. Helping allies buy US technology has bipartisan support. In May, Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen and Republican Senator Pete Ricketts proposed subsidising allies' US technology purchases through a US$250 million fund, and the State Department must work with Congress on it. Democrats have been pressing Nvidia over export controls.

Seven months later the hub development agreement is still unsigned. Taiwanese firms are interested but holding back pending US signing and follow-through. The Philippine development authority pledged no power or water shortages, and the agreement must specify electricity and water needs and costs.

The Department of Information and Communications Technology is pushing for wider use of artificial intelligence among micro, small and medium enterprises. Secretary Robert Joseph "Jay" de Claro made the push at a forum on AI and connectivity held in Makati City on Thursday, 26 November 2026. The event was the 2026 ROK-PHL-ASEAN AI+ Connectivity Forum.

About 99 percent of Philippine businesses are MSMEs, and the DICT says barriers to AI adoption include the cost of technology, limited digital skills and unequal internet access. The ASEAN Leaders Declaration on AI-powered MSME Growth, adopted at the 49th ASEAN Summit, promotes affordable AI tools, cloud services and training. It also calls for improved connectivity, AI skills and responsible use. The Philippines holds the 2026 ASEAN chairship.

De Claro said AI should not be reserved for big firms. "AI must not become an advantage reserved only for large companies. It must also become an opportunity for our smallest businesses," he said. He said AI can help MSMEs with customer service, daily operations and reaching more customers. He said the opportunities they create, not only the technologies they develop or the infrastructure they build, should measure the success of this cooperation.

Executive Order 131 adopts the Philippine AI Governance Framework and creates the National Artificial Intelligence Council. The DICT lists connectivity, capability and trust as its priorities. In partnership with the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in the Philippines, the Stratbase Institute organized the forum.

stories.Headline: Vietnam law makes AI deployers liable for harm even when fully compliant
stories.Summary:
VCI Legal, a law firm, has published an article on who pays when an AI system causes harm despite compliance. Vietnam's Law on Artificial Intelligence No. 134/2025/QH15, in force since 1 March 2026, imposes strict liability on deployers, the firm wrote. Under the law, a deployer must compensate an injured party even when it has fully complied with its obligations.

The law sets three risk levels: high, medium and low. The provider classifies the system before use and notifies the Ministry of Science and Technology through a single-window AI portal. Decree No. 142/2026/ND-CP and the Prime Minister's Decision No. 33/2026/QD-TTg key the high-risk list to purpose and usage conditions. VCI Legal gives credit scoring as an example of high-risk classification: a system whose final approval or refusal is used directly to extend credit, with no independent credit officer approval, and where the loan meets a State Bank of Viet Nam value criterion.

Article 14 requires human oversight design, technical records and logs, and preservation of the deployer's ability to intervene, and the deployer must operate within the classified purpose. Article 11 requires labelling of AI-generated imitation video. While the deployer is made liable to the injured party by Article 29(2), exemptions are set by Article 29(3). The deployer may seek reimbursement from the provider, depending on the parties' agreement, and VCI Legal advises that contracts specify reimbursement timing and amounts.

Health, education and financial systems get an 18-month period, and other pre-existing systems get 12 months. In the three sectors, listed high-risk systems that pre-date 15 August 2026 must comply before 1 September 2027, and in the remaining sectors before 1 March 2027. Systems starting within six months of 15 August 2026 must comply before 1 March 2027. VCI Legal notes that identical lending systems may face different deadlines.

stories.Headline: AI tools drive sharp rise in public records requests across US agencies
stories.Summary:
Kyle Rowe, the town clerk of Panton, Vermont, handled budgets, taxes, zoning and elections for the town of 660 people, and he also fielded public records requests. Last year, SmartProcure, doing business as GovSpend, which had sought all purchasing records yearly, began asking quarterly. Other companies sought specific records, such as road flares, in targeted inquiries that came monthly or more. Rowe, who is no longer town clerk, said of the requests: "it feels like I'm doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers' time."

Similar experiences have been reported across the United States. Data brokers have mined public records for decades, but venture-backed startups have raised over $100 million to turn those records into AI-powered sales "signals." AI tools make it easier to draft public records requests, and many places have seen double-digit annual increases in requests. The AI-drafted requests are longer and broader in scope, while the offices answering them lack added staff or budget, and some states have passed laws easing the denial of requests.

The US Freedom of Information Act passed in 1966, and every state has its own records law. In 2016, a study titled "FOIA, Inc." found that commercial requesters made 79% to 96% of federal requests at agencies studied, including the EPA and FDA; it was published by Margaret Kwoka, a recent member of the FOIA Advisory Committee and a law professor at Ohio State University. Kwoka said the market is now for "much more sophisticated and integrated database products."

SmartProcure pioneered the model 15 years ago. Trip Colden, the chief operating officer of GovSpend, said requests are "handled by real people with long-standing relationships." Starbridge raised $52 million in a Series A led by Craft Ventures, the firm of David Sacks, a former White House AI and crypto czar; Starbridge describes its mission as getting "the best technology into the hands of public leaders." Pursuit raised $25.5 million from investors including Bill Gurley and Jack Altman and describes "an industrial-scale FOIA operation"; Mike Vichich, its CEO and cofounder, said "competition is what saves taxpayers money."

Mark Zurada, chief operating officer of PinPoint Analytics, said the company sent up to 2,000 requests per day and now sends closer to 500. SmartProcure and Pursuit send about 180,000 requests yearly. NationGraph, which serves midsize vendors such as janitorial providers, claims about 10,000 requests per day and did not respond to comment requests. Company requests typically use templates rather than AI, and AI is used to standardize and analyze the returned records.

Chautauqua County, New York, hired a paralegal this summer after its requests doubled; a county attorney blamed ChatGPT use and resellers. Sarah Alanis, chief deputy clerk of Ann Arbor, Michigan, said requests rose from 581 in 2021 to 937 last year, and that "our new normal is high." Federal agencies received a record 1.7 million requests last year, a rise the New York Times attributed partly to AI and also to mass filings by the Heritage Foundation and immigrant records requests.

At least 29% of requests were at least partly AI-written, according to David Cuillier, director of the Brechner Freedom of Information Project at the University of Florida, who ran the US Department of Education's July request log through an AI detector. Those requests were twice as long, and 83% sought long lists of records. Liz Wagenseller, executive director of the Pennsylvania Office of Open Records, said AI activity is "breaking records every month"; appeals there were about 3,000 in 2021, just under 4,000 in 2025 and are projected at 6,000 this year. Wagenseller said chatbots "always give [people] encouragement to try." Some filings contain hallucinated legal citations, and one included a user's prompt to Claude.

One-fifth of federal agencies use AI or machine learning for records searches, and the Washington Post reported that DHS uses AI to speed redactions. CivicPlus, whose NextRequest platform handles over a million requests yearly, uses captchas to screen out bots. Jane Snyder, CivicPlus's chief marketing officer, said a captcha "doesn't determine whether a person used AI to help draft a request." CivicPlus counts over 20 state and federal measures this year, including a California measure signed in September declaring AI systems not "members of the public."

A stalled Pennsylvania bill would allow denial of suspected AI requests. In Allen County, Indiana, officials described "suspiciously non-human" requests that consumed up to 20 hours weekly of staff time. An Indiana law took effect July 1 letting agencies charge out-of-state requesters, prioritize residents and deny suspected scraping requests. Adams County, Indiana, banned commercial use of records in March, after requests rose from about one weekly to as many as 10; they have settled at one to five since the state law. Clayton Lengerich, the county attorney, said the rules don't affect "any individual requester's ability to keep their local municipality accountable."

Congress amended FOIA in 1986 to charge commercial requesters more, but fee rules are rarely applied due to exceptions. Kwoka said "It costs more for the agencies to collect the fees than it's worth in fees"; agencies recoup less than 5% of costs from commercial requesters, and the FDA spent $33.6 million and recouped $328,000 in one year. Kwoka advocates "affirmative disclosure." The EPA has posted property contamination records online, and California's Open FI$Cal portal publishes spending data, though such portals lack the full contracts that sales-tech firms seek.

stories.Headline: Ribbon helps Verizon retire legacy voice networks to free facilities for edge AI
stories.Summary:
Ribbon Communications is helping Verizon modernize its voice networks, work that the vendor says could free up facilities for AI infrastructure. Bruce McLelland, CEO of Ribbon Communications, said the modernization programs have a longer-term dimension given the investment underway in AI infrastructure. Ribbon, an optical and IP vendor headquartered in Massachusetts, is a key supplier to Verizon.

Verizon is retiring legacy TDM-based voice services and discontinuing copper in nine US states, which frees facilities for edge AI. Legacy voice equipment required significant space and power, and Verizon is shrinking its power and space footprints. McLelland said Ribbon expects a higher deployment or migration rate in 2027, though planning for that year is still early. He said Ribbon is ready to assist Verizon in the Frontier footprint and that "We'll see what approach they take in the Frontier footprint." The FCC approved the copper discontinuation after a two-month pause, and the article noted concerns from affected consumers.

TNS announced a partnership with Ribbon in September, and TNS Hosted Cloud Connect incorporates Ribbon technology as a managed cloud voice alternative. McLelland said Ribbon is also focused on expanding the addressable market for its voice network modernization solutions, which gives smaller operators a cost-effective modernization path. Ribbon's IP routing shipments grew about 35% and exceeded total optical sales, and the company won two new Tier 2 service provider customers and a new win with a large civilian federal agency. McLelland said "This was our best third quarter ever and the second-highest quarterly revenue performance in the U.S."

For the third quarter, Ribbon reported IP Optical revenue of $96 million, up 17% sequentially, and Cloud & Edge revenue of $123 million, up 11%. Total revenue was $219 million, up 14% sequentially, adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to $27 million, service provider revenue rose 15% sequentially and US sales rose more than 150% year over year. Ribbon forecast fourth-quarter 2026 revenue of $233 million to $247 million. Eric Marmurek, CFO of Ribbon Communications, said "We expect continued sequential growth and increased profitability in the fourth quarter, led primarily by our Cloud and Edge segment." The article also cited Ribbon agreements with Google worth over $1 billion and with AWS worth over $2 billion, and noted over 500,000 route miles of fiber freed across North America.

stories.Headline: Child Online Africa urges Ghana to put child welfare first in school AI plans
stories.Summary:
Child Online Africa, an advocacy organisation, issued a statement on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, urging a human-centred approach to integrating artificial intelligence into Ghana's basic school curriculum. The statement, signed by Executive Director Awo Aidam Amenyah, welcomed the government's ambition but asked for deeper consideration of how AI enters classrooms. It called for a clear distinction between AI literacy and AI dependency, warning that dependency may come before children develop independent reasoning skills.

The organisation proposed nine measures for the Ministry of Education, whose plans cover AI, robotics, coding and electronics for Kindergarten to Primary Six. It sought a child-centred AI-in-education policy, independent research on developmental appropriateness, and age-appropriate standards for school AI use. It also asked for continuous professional development for teachers, stronger child online protection and data privacy standards, and equitable access to electricity, devices and connectivity. It called for piloting in selected schools before a nationwide rollout, the involvement of children, parents, teachers and experts, and measurable indicators on learning outcomes.

The statement raised concerns about teacher preparedness, children's personal data protection and unequal digital access, warning that rural children with limited electricity and internet may be left behind. According to Amenyah, "The question is how, when, why and under what conditions AI should be introduced into their learning environments," not "whether our children should learn about artificial intelligence." She also said, "Technology must serve the child. The child must never become a servant of technology." Child Online Africa denied that its position was opposition to technological innovation and offered to join national dialogue and policy consultations.

The Ministry of Education announced the plans on X during the 2026 National Education Week and Evidence Summit, as part of Ghana's broader digital education transformation agenda. The ministry has not publicly responded to the statement.

stories.Headline: Montgomery County schools draft rules letting teachers decide classroom AI use
stories.Summary:
Montgomery County Public Schools released an 11-page draft regulation on classroom artificial intelligence on Nov. 17, Bethesda Magazine reported. Under the draft, teachers decide whether, when and how approved AI tools are used, and the district sets no systemwide ban or blanket mandate. The draft allows AI for lesson planning and administrative work. It also places limits on how student and staff data may be used.

The draft bars personally identifiable data from going into unapproved AI tools and prohibits AI from collecting biometric, behavioral or location data. Vendors would be barred from training their models on district data, and cloud and generative AI must anonymize data as far as possible. The draft prohibits AI deepfakes, voice cloning, misinformation and misrepresentation. Students and staff must cite and acknowledge their AI use, and AI material cannot stand in for original work. No dishonesty finding may rest solely on AI detection, and no automated system may make final decisions on grading, placement, tracking or special education eligibility without human review.

The regulation builds on Board of Education Policy IGS on Educational Technology, which was adopted May 21, 2026 and directed the superintendent to write implementing rules. AI tools are vetted with a Maryland State Department of Education rubric, with at least 60 days for standard digital tool vetting. The district's community update said the goal is "comprehensive procedures governing the ethical, responsible, equitable and secure use of AI." District spokesperson Liliana López said "protecting students while ensuring AI supports rather than replaces meaningful teaching and learning is the priority." López also said Google gave MCPS no information on its search and AI changes, after Google said it would restrict search if districts reject its AI tools.

Betsy Tao, head of the MCCPTA Technology Committee, called the technology "kryptonite to learning" and said leaving decisions to teachers risks inconsistent enforcement. She urged the incoming school board to act strongly on AI policy. The draft also calls for AI literacy learning opportunities for students, with library media specialists serving as building-level literacy contacts. Daniel Umana, manager of Montgomery College's Digital Learning Center, said students should interrogate AI-generated answers.

Catherine Bucsa, a Wootton High School senior and online editor-in-chief of the student newspaper, wrote a September op-ed criticizing staff AI-created art and posters and favors regulation by use and student age rather than a ban. The DMV Parent Coalition seeks a moratorium on student-facing AI. Lawsuits allege AI tools harmed student mental health, including a suit alleging a 13-year-old planned suicide after using a school laptop chatbot, and a Silver Spring former student at John F. Kennedy High School used a school Chromebook chatbot for homework and then as a confidante. Frederick County banned AI for students in all grades, The Baltimore Sun reported. Residents can comment on the draft through Friday, Dec. 18, before a final version is issued.

Articles.Title: MCPS Draft AI Rules Give Teachers Classroom Control - Hoodline

stories.headline_source: MCPS Draft AI Rules Give Teachers Classroom Control

stories.Headline: Papa John’s AI agent makes UK’s first cardless payment under FCA sandbox
stories.Summary:
A Papa John’s AI agent made the first purchase by an AI agent in the UK using cardless payment technology, ordering nine mini margherita pizzas on Friday 27 November 2026, the Guardian reported. The order was reported at 04.53 EST, and the article was last modified at 11.51 EST.

The purchase was part of trials in a sandbox regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority. The agent was given permission to access a bank account, with a strict mandate set with Lloyds Bank covering a maximum spend limit per transaction and a maximum spend limit per month. No account security information was shared.

Francesco Simoneschi, chief executive of the London-based payment specialist TrueLayer, said: “We completed this payment transaction with Papa John’s with no account numbers, no password [and] handled with the highest possible security profile.” He also said: “This is possibly the last Black Friday as we know it.”

The FCA warned AI agent developers earlier this week. Meta’s Muse assistant launched in the UK on Tuesday and pays using the customer’s bank card.

stories.Headline: AI-designed stimulation patterns help a blind man perceive shapes with a 96-electrode visual cortex implant
stories.Summary:
The flashes, known as phosphenes, came from an experimental implant with 96 electrodes. In 2024, researchers from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich and Miguel Hernández University traveled to Spain to work with him. The implant was intended to last six months.

The device is a visual cortical prosthesis, often called a bionic eye, and it targets the visual cortex rather than the eye itself. An AI deep learning model was trained on the man's brain responses, and patterns designed by the AI improved accuracy. According to Fox News, the AI-designed patterns also used less electrical current. Brain activity better predicted the sights the man reported.

Michael Beyeler, an associate professor at UC Santa Barbara, said the technology should serve the user. "Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around," he said. The findings were published in the journal Neuron.

The man saw flashes and shapes, not normal sight, and he was the only participant in the experiment. No reading or face recognition was demonstrated. According to Fox News, more research is needed on other people.

stories.Headline: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims an unreleased Claude version proves the Riemann hypothesis
stories.Summary:
Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, claimed last Friday to have proved the Riemann hypothesis, a problem open since 1859, according to the Guardian. The proof was produced with an unreleased version of the Claude chatbot. Computers can validate the Alpöge-Claude proof.

Steven Strogatz, a mathematician at Cornell University, said students ask him, "What's the point if the AI can do math better than any human being?" He fears AI discoveries may defy human understanding, and compared explaining AI to "trying to teach calculus to his own dog."

The Bank of England warned that unreleased models could break encryption, which safeguards global finance and communications. There are cryptosphere rumours of a breach within two years. Marcus du Sautoy, a mathematician at Oxford University, wondered on BBC Radio 4 whether the breakthrough had already occurred secretly, as discoveries occur inside privately owned AI labs. Donald Trump intervened earlier this year to restrain the spread of frontier models, and most states lack the expertise to assess AI risks.

In a landmark 1965 paper, the British mathematician IJ Good wrote that "the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention that man need ever make." Leading AI firms pursue such a machine.

stories.Headline: Sweet Home district builds AI bus routing tool that cuts six-hour task to minutes
stories.Summary:
Superintendent Mike Ginestre of the Sweet Home Central School District, outside Buffalo, N.Y., said the district built its own AI routing tool, which is used only by the transportation office and by no students. He said a task that once took six hours for a single after-school bus run now takes minutes, and that student seat sign-up lead time has fallen from two weeks. "We've reduced it into minutes," Ginestre said. Ginestre said the district's staff face heavy paperwork. "We have so many reports to file, and we do all of this work by hand," he said.

According to edtechmagazine.com, 69% of public schools reported difficulty filling nonteaching positions in the 2024-25 year. Sweet Home is piloting AI coworkers with TechBuffalo, a nonprofit led by the article's author, and Radial Ventures, a Buffalo-based venture studio, the outlet reported. A performance review, a human supervisor and a job description are what each AI coworker has. TechBuffalo's Innovation Fellowship ran from April to June 2026, and 12 teachers took part, according to the outlet. Fellows were given direct access to a frontier model and built apps and AI agents for their own work, and they designed student experiences with faculty from the University at Buffalo Graduate School of Education.

A 2025 Gallup survey of 2,232 public school teachers found that those using AI at least weekly saved 5.9 hours a week, the equivalent of six weeks per school year, the outlet reported. A 2026 Gallup survey found 82% of teachers had no formal AI guidance. The national debate over AI in schools has centered on students since 2022, the outlet reported. In a study of nearly 1,000 high school math students, Hamsa Bastani, a researcher and associate professor at the Wharton School, found scores 17% lower for students who practiced with a standard chatbot, while a purpose-built version largely prevented the learning loss, according to the outlet. Ginestre said, "We got into teaching to be with students and to partner with parents."

stories.Headline: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claims a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis
stories.Summary:
Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, claims that a Claude-assisted solution of the Riemann hypothesis was reached in November 2026, according to DW. The Riemann hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and has been open since 1859.

Andrea Asperti, a computer science professor at the University of Bologna, attributed the gains to model size, training data and methods. He said AI now checks its work, corrects mistakes and uses math software. "These relatively incremental technological improvements have resulted in qualitative leaps in intellectual capabilities," he said. He also said that "solving open mathematical problems requires a considerable degree of creativity: it is not simply a matter of retrieving existing knowledge or reproducing known arguments."

Ken Ono, a mathematics professor at the University of Virginia, said Gemini once claimed that 9.11 is greater than 9.8. "But make no mistake, those errors are very rare today," he said. Kevin Buzzard, a mathematician at Imperial College London, said AI found a counterexample in an algebraic geometry problem. "I had thought about the problem myself and could see what the difficulties were. AI cut through them," he said.

Ono said that a model can draw on tens of thousands of research papers in pure mathematics. "It might be 30 or 40 mathematicians you would have to put in a room before you could assemble this proof," he said. Ono, who has trained 35 PhD students, said: "Make no mistake. In the year 2026, the ground shifted beneath the entire edifice of the world of human mathematical research."

Buzzard said: "Now you can prove a theorem by pressing a button, so we need new methods." Ono said he did not think a model trained on mathematics and physics known by the end of the 19th century would spin up Einstein's theory of relativity on its own. "I don't think we've seen that sort of creative spark, that sort of ability yet," he said. Buzzard is setting up a lab on understanding, explaining and defending proofs.

Articles.Title: AI vs. Riemann hypothesis: How AI went from fluffing simple sums to cracking the hardest math problems

stories.headline_source: AI vs. Riemann hypothesis: How AI went from fluffing simple sums to cracking the hardest math problems

stories.Headline: Perplexity launches Time Machine AI to train forecasting models on archived web data
stories.Summary:
Perplexity has launched a Time Machine AI feature, the company's Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas said. The feature lets developers train and evaluate forecasting models using archived internet data from a chosen date. It blocks information published after that cutoff, which is set through the Search and Context APIs. Only webpages that existed on or before the chosen date are included in the results.

The feature offers archived snapshots going back up to 365 days. Perplexity stores copies of indexed webpages, and the Context API retrieves archived text rather than the live site. The company says this addresses the leakage of event outcomes in forecasting tests. In one case, the model GLM-5.3 Flash, trained on Polymarket questions, saw its score rise from 0.77 to 0.80, against a Polymarket market odds score of 0.79.

The feature works with existing API keys and endpoints at no additional surcharge, according to the company. Search costs $5 per 1,000 requests and Context costs $1 per 1,000 URLs fetched. "Perplexity has launched a new Time Machine artificial intelligence (AI) feature," Srinivas said. TechGig published its report on Nov 27, 2026.

stories.Headline: Thomson Reuters combines US and Chinese AI models to lower costs and protect intellectual property
stories.Summary:
Thomson Reuters plans to launch the Thomson 1.1 AI model by the end of 2026. According to techgig.com, the tool will combine open-source models including Google Gemma from the US and Z.ai GLM from China. The model is intended to help clients with mid-tier tasks such as tax advice.

The company is investing $40 million to develop the system. It will use under 5 per cent of current tokens and is designed to increase control over intellectual property and lower AI costs. While complex tasks will still use Anthropic and OpenAI, the new model replaces the Alibaba Qwen used in Thomson 1.0.

Chief Technology Officer Joel Hron said the project shows "AI sovereignty actually looks like in practice." JetBrains said the initiative "aims to extend GoLand's language intelligence beyond the IntelliJ Platform, making it accessible to a broader range of developers and workflows."

JetBrains is gathering user feedback on performance and feature requests through the GoLand Slack channel or a dedicated form. stories.Headline: Anthropic weighs latency and avoided incidents over project length in engineer promotions
stories.Summary:
Anthropic is rethinking how it promotes its engineers, according to Katelyn Lesse, the company's head of platform engineering. Lesse discussed the change on a podcast released on Wednesday, and an article on it was published on 27 November 2026. The length of a project is now a less useful measure when deciding on promotions. The team is instead weighing lower latency and avoided incidents.

Impact remains the ultimate success measure, Lesse said. "Impact" remains the ultimate measure of success, she said. Impact increasingly means coordination, which includes aligning people and agents. The implementation portion of engineering work has shrunk.

Anthropic is also experimenting with interview formats that use coding agents. These interviews test candidates using coding agents, including reviewing code written by an agent and building systems with an agent's assistance. Some candidates struggled with traditional hand-coding rounds. The team is seeking the best way to gauge proficiency with AI tools.

Work that once took years is now done in months, and Claude Code is used by hundreds of thousands of workers globally.
