stories.Headline: XEBO.ai raises $10.5 Mn Series A from Emirates Growth Fund to expand customer experience platform
stories.Summary:
XEBO.ai, a Dubai-headquartered experience management company, has raised $10.5 Mn (around ₹97.1 Cr) in a Series A round, according to Inc42. Emirates Growth Fund, described by the outlet as a UAE flagship growth equity investor, was the sole investor in the round. The company was founded in 2017 and was previously known as Survey2Connect before rebranding in late 2023. Yash Sultania, cofounder and CEO of XEBO.ai, said "around 30-40% of the investment will go towards product development."

That work covers voice analytics, digital analytics and agentic AI. Around 30% of the capital is earmarked for existing markets, which include the GCC, Africa, Asia Pacific and India. The remainder will fund new geographies, with North America a key focus, and cofounder Anand Nigam has relocated to the US to lead that expansion. XEBO.ai serves more than 350 enterprises across over 10 industries, with clients including HSBC Middle East, Emirates Airlines, Starbucks, H&M, Dubai Properties, Abu Dhabi government, Tata AIG and Mahindra Group.

Around 200 clients are in the Middle East and more than 50 are in Europe and North America. The company runs an annual subscription model with contracts ranging from $10,000 to $200,000, competes with Qualtrics and Medallia, and employs more than 100 people, around 80% of them based in India, where its operations include a Noida office. Sultania said "We are looking to reach $100 Mn in ARR over the next four to five years." The startup is in talks with other potential investors and may raise a Series B in the next two years, according to Inc42.

stories.Headline: Liu Yang leads a team in releasing OmniV-Bench to test MLLMs on 360-degree video understanding
stories.Summary:
A team of ten authors led by first author Liu Yang has introduced OmniV-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on omnidirectional video spatio-temporal understanding. The work was posted on 27 November 2026 as an arXiv preprint, identifier 2611.31022. The benchmark uses 360-degree field-of-view videos and covers 11 fine-grained tasks. The co-authors are Huiyu Duan, Yixuan Gao, Sirui Liu, Lu Liu, Zhaolin Cai, Ke Gu, Xiongkuo Min, Xiaoping Zhang and Guangtao Zhai.

OmniV-Bench is built on 4,123 high-quality omnidirectional videos and 8,923 human-annotated question-answer pairs. Its 11 tasks fall into three categories: general, spatial and spatio-temporal. The authors also propose OmniV-Harness, an agentic harness that uses viewpoint-guided evidence initialization and adaptive tool use. The authors say both resources will be released upon publication.

According to the authors, omnidirectional videos capture dynamic environments with full spatial context, and applications include virtual reality, augmented reality and embodied intelligence. They add that MLLM understanding of immersive 360-degree scenes is largely unexplored. The benchmark experiments show that spatio-temporal complexity challenges MLLMs, the authors report, while the harness consistently improves immersive spatio-temporal reasoning.

Articles.Title: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?

stories.headline_source: OmniV-Bench: Can MLLMs Comprehend Immersive Spatio-temporal Scenes?

stories.Headline: Researchers propose hierarchical randomized neural networks to find multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations
stories.Summary:
Jingying Hu, Jiao Li, Yufeng Xu and Jinyong Ying have proposed a new method for finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations, built on randomized neural networks. The work, dated November 27, 2026, is an arXiv preprint numbered 2611.30010. Finding multiple solutions is a fundamental task in scientific computing.

The method addresses three aspects: initialization, optimization and an acceleration technique. A characteristic matrix is formed from basis functions and sampling points, and singular value decomposition is used to find weakly variant search directions. A new algorithm generates effective initial candidates, and a deflated Gauss-Newton method with an exponential deflation operator is used, adapted from work by A. Riley and others published in SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing, volume 47, issue 5, 2025, pages A2963 to A2987.

A local error estimate is given for a particular solution, depending on the hidden-layer neurons and the sampling points. A new multilevel method based on hierarchical networks accelerates computation and improves accuracy, with relative errors reaching 10^-16 and, in the best case, less than one-tenth of the computational cost. The method preserves the inherent symmetries of solutions and uses no a priori information. Several numerical tests are reported.

Articles.Title: Hierarchical randomized neural networks for efficiently and accurately finding multiple solutions of semilinear elliptic equations

stories.Headline: Lam Research wins new advanced packaging tool orders as AI chip demand rises
stories.Summary:
Lam Research Corporation, a semiconductor equipment maker, is finding new opportunities in advanced semiconductor packaging as demand for AI and high-performance computing chips rises and complex packaging connects multiple components. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the company saw demand for etch, deposition and plating equipment. Through-silicon-via applications for advanced logic and HBM brought four new positions across multiple customers to its Syndion platform. Its Striker ALD tools won multiple TSV liner applications, while VECTOR and TEOS 3D won bonding film and inter-die gap filling applications.

Panel sizes from 300-by-300 millimeters to 600-by-600 millimeters were offered, and panel plating systems went to more than 20 customers worldwide, Lam said. The Kallisto platform supports uniform plating and is positioned for interest in glass-core substrates. According to the article, Lam Research "expects Lam Research's panel-level packaging market share to eventually exceed its already strong position in wafer-level packaging." The company reported revenues of $8.22 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 54% year over year, with foundry at 46% of systems revenues, up from 44% the previous quarter.

The article notes that panel-level packaging adoption will take time and that competitors are also developing panel-level packaging equipment. Applied Materials, Inc. is expanding its advanced packaging business and reported record fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 revenues of $10.41 billion, up 53% year over year. Applied Materials said on its earnings call that "demand for advanced chips continues to outstrip supply," and it expects advanced packaging revenues up about 90% in calendar 2026. Onto Innovation Inc., which competes in inspection and process-control equipment, reported record third-quarter 2026 revenues of $409.7 million, up 88% year over year, with its Dragonfly G5 and Firefly inspection systems.

Onto's Advanced Packaging and Specialty Devices segment was slightly over half of third-quarter revenues and up 35% sequentially, and Onto expects Advanced Packaging revenues up more than 80% in 2026, with growth split between 2.5D logic and HBM. Onto's backlog exceeded $1.3 billion. Lam Research shares are up 19.7% year to date, while the Zacks Electronics, Semiconductors industry is down 14.8% year to date. Lam's forward price-to-earnings ratio is 17.57, against an industry average of 8.31. The Zacks Consensus Estimate projects fiscal 2027 revenues up 49.9% year over year and fiscal 2028 revenues up 18.9%, with fiscal 2027 earnings up 65.2% and fiscal 2028 earnings up 23.7%. Fiscal 2027 estimates were revised upward in the past 30 days and the fiscal 2028 consensus over the past 60 days. Lam Research carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), and the article says it must keep delivering reliable equipment to gain share.

stories.Headline: Authors post HiCal, an offline calibration method that refines HiF4 quantization encoding at three scale levels
stories.Summary:
Zhiyuan Zhang, Yanzhao Li, Hui Dong, Sifan Cheng, Mingen Zheng and Hui Wang, the authors, posted HiCal on arXiv on November 27, 2026, under identifier 2611.32624. HiCal is an offline calibration method for HiF4 quantization that refines encoding decisions at three scale levels. It calibrates rounding bias for the Level-1 E6M2 scale and optimizes scale-extension thresholds at Levels 2 and 3.

HiF4 uses a hierarchical scale encoding scheme with a global E6M2 scale and two binary scale extensions. The authors say the conventional rounding rule and fixed thresholds may miss tensor statistics. HiCal sets its calibration parameters offline and fixes them during inference, so no per-block multi-candidate scale search is needed, and the original deterministic HiF4 encoding is preserved.

The authors report a quantization MSE reduction of 9.91% to 23.50% across five synthetic and real activation distributions tested, including a 13.00% MSE reduction on real Qwen3-8B activations. In end-to-end evaluations on six benchmarks, they report an average-score gain of 0.91 percentage points on Qwen3-8B and 1.25 percentage points on Qwen3-30B-A3B.

Articles.Title: HiCal: Offline Calibration for Hierarchical Scale Encoding in Accurate HiF4 Quantization

stories.Summary:

(FORM) is benefiting from rising demand for high-bandwidth memory as AI infrastructure expansion increases test complexity, according to a Zacks article published on Yahoo Finance on November 24, 2026. The growth is driven by the company's Probe Cards business, with HBM testing remaining a key driver. Its SmartMatrix DRAM architecture for HBM final stack testing has completed tests on HBM4 stacks above 10 gigabits per second. The article notes consensus earnings growth of 155% year over year for 2026 and 30% for 2027, and gives FORM a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). stories.Headline: TSMC's CoWoS capacity stays fully booked as orders shift to ASE and Amkor
stories.Summary:
TSMC's CoWoS capacity is fully booked, and orders are being diverted to ASE and Amkor, according to research firm DIGITIMES. The firm estimates that high-end cloud AI accelerator shipments will reach 26 million units in 2027. It says 85.8% of those shipments will use TSMC packaging that year, with CoWoS-L accounting for 54.6% of total shipments. DIGITIMES estimates combined CoWoS-like demand for ASE and Amkor at 466,000 wafers in 2027, 5.5 times their 2026 level.

TSMC's CoWoS customer demand is put at 2.165 million wafers in 2027, requiring an average monthly supply of 180,000 wafers. Broadcom and MediaTek together account for 393,000 wafers of CoWoS demand that year, while NVIDIA's incremental CoWoS demand is 400,000 wafers. By the end of 2027, ASE's monthly CoWoS-like capacity is expected to reach 45,000 wafers, and Amkor's 20,000 wafers. Weng Shu-ting, a DIGITIMES analyst, said of server CPUs: "server CPUs use a multi-chiplet architecture, raising requirements for die-to-die interconnect bandwidth while keeping packaging costs in check."

AMD's server CPU Venice uses ASE FOCoS-Bridge, SPIL FO-EB and Amkor S-Connect, the report says. Lower-cost options include Intel EMIB and Powertech PiFO. Amazon's Trainium 3 is to adopt EMIB-M in the first half of 2027, Google's TPU v9 is to adopt EMIB-T in the first half of 2028, and AMD's Venice is to adopt Powertech PiFO in the second half of 2027. What to watch next is the pace of TSMC's CoWoS expansion against demand, and ASE's progress on CoWoS-like capacity.

stories.Headline: Presidential Office Weighs Making AI Refuse to Solve Exam Questions
stories.Summary:
Lee Hae-min, senior presidential secretary for AI future planning, said the presidential office is weighing an option to make AI refuse to solve exam questions. The option would specify that solving the questions is illegal, he said. He made the remarks on the 27th on MBC Radio's "Kim Jong-bae's Focus." According to Lee, "to specify that solving the questions is illegal, so that AI itself makes a reasonable refusal."

The method states exam paper facts to the AI, Lee said. He cited an example of a Korean-language exam paper with certain hours and a certain date. Doing so is punishable under the Higher Education Act. Lee said "many tips and proposals are coming in from across the country."

A technical review with the Ministry of Science and ICT is planned, along with verification through experiments. Countermeasures will be drawn up across all ministries. When the host raised multinational cooperation with AI companies, Lee said "Korea is trying to do that first."

At a meeting of senior secretaries and advisers at Cheong Wa Dae on Sept. 3, Lee Won-joo, presidential adviser for national strategic investment, addressed a U.S. proposal for a 15% tariff ceiling for Korea and a U.S. push to raise semiconductor cluster investment in the Honam region. Lee Hae-min said "There was an initial sense of relief, but we are watching closely," as the U.S. plans to regulate AI data center investment outside the United States. He said it "does not seem appropriate to talk about the stock market," and that "Demand is in fact visibly strong."

"AI for All," also called National Secretary, is set to launch next month. Three consortiums are building its features.

stories.Headline: ExpGuard assesses and repairs risky experiences for long-horizon LLM agents
stories.Summary:
Eleven authors, including Yuzhou Chen, Licheng Pan, Zhixuan Chu, Yunsheng Lu, Yichen Sun, Han Zheng, Yan Wang, Bingyu Zhu, Haiwen Hong, Longtao Huang and Kui Ren, published ExpGuard, a framework for assessing the risk of experiences used by long-horizon LLM agents, in an arXiv preprint dated November 27, 2026, under identifier 2611.32085.

ExpGuard performs retrieval-triggered risk assessment and online repair, predicting the risks of attack and task failure before an experience is reused. It relies on a task-conditioned heterogeneous graph that integrates semantics, provenance and execution dependencies, along with matched counterfactual replays of experiences that compare original and neutralized counterparts. Risk labels are drawn from differences in attack success and in task completion. The framework repairs high-risk experiences at retrieval and re-predicts risks before they enter the active context.

The authors describe three challenges in assessing corruption risks: modeling provenance and dependencies, task-conditioned risk learning, and online inference repair. Long-horizon LLM agents distill past trajectories into experiences that can be reused across tasks, and corrupted experiences can let harmful instructions persist, according to the preprint.

Extensive experiments reported in the preprint demonstrated the framework's effectiveness, the authors said, showing both the identification of risky experiences and defense against experience corruption.

Articles.Title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience

stories.Headline: Ambarella prepares to tape out second 2nm AI chip with Samsung
stories.Summary:
Ambarella, a U.S. chip designer and Samsung foundry customer, is finalizing the design of its second 2nm chip and is supplying customers with samples of its first, which was developed with Samsung. The company said on an earnings call on 24 November 2026 that it plans to tape out the second chip shortly, a step that hands the final design to the manufacturer and moves it closer to mass production. Mass-production revenue from the first chip is expected in the second half of 2027, and details of the second chip are to be unveiled at CES in early 2027.

Ambarella designs AI inference systems-on-chips for edge devices that handle video, including CCTV cameras, vehicles and drones. The company is fabless, and Samsung is its main manufacturing partner, with most of its SoCs made at Samsung plants in Austin, Texas, and South Korea, according to an SEC filing cited by the Seoul Economic Daily. The relationship began in 2010, when Samsung made 45nm image-processing chips for digital cameras, and has expanded through 5nm and 4nm to 2nm AI chips. Ambarella previously worked with Taiwan's TSMC and strengthened its Samsung ties after a 2025 capacity struggle in which Nvidia, AMD and Apple took production priority.

Recognizing and processing visual information with AI on camera-equipped devices, the CV8 ,  the first commercial 2nm product ,  is used in 360-degree cameras and high-resolution videoconferencing equipment, and Ambarella began designing the CV8 two years ago, completed its tape-out in January 2026 and produced a first prototype around June 2026, with mass production set for the second half of 2027. Fermi Wang, Ambarella's chief executive, described the Samsung relationship in September 2026 as an "exclusive partnership" and said on the earnings call that "the second 2nm chip will be taped out soon" and that there would be "additional information at CES 2027." Samsung and Ambarella also collaborate in the automotive SoC field, the Seoul Economic Daily reported in an article by Lee Suk-jin that was AI-translated from Korean, with foreign-source quotes that may not match the original wording.

stories.Headline: Employees cannot reliably tell an AI CEO bot from the real CEO in a field study
stories.Summary:
An AI-created "CEO bot," a combination of chief executive officer and robot, is the subject of a field study run three years ago, according to en.sedaily.com. Several technology companies are experimenting with AI versions of executives, and these digital leaders answer questions, join meetings and communicate with staff. In the study, employees were asked to guess whether instructions and feedback came from a person or from AI. The employees could not reliably tell the CEO from the AI.

Employees rated answers they believed came from AI as less helpful, and they marked down the actual CEO's answers when they assumed AI had produced them. The article describes the concept of an AI trained on a person's digital traces as a "codified self." This codified self reproduces a portion of the human capital that surfaces in an organization, but it is not a complete digital copy of a person. Its codified expertise can be deployed at multiple interaction points at the same time, as when a senior engineer assists expatriate staff worldwide without meetings.

The codified self creates an asset whose ownership between employee and employer is ambiguous, and there is no answer yet on what rights employees have over systems built from their expertise. An organizational digital twin, built on proprietary data and AI agents, lets managers test reorganization alternatives in simulation. Digital twins were previously used for physical assets and are now entering the organizational domain. According to the article, digital twins will go further and replicate successful CEOs.

Articles.Title: Will AI's 'CEO Bot' Work? - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.headline_source: Will AI's 'CEO Bot' Work?

stories.Headline: Intellivix demonstrates Argos quadrupedal patrol robot for construction site safety at 2026 expo
stories.Summary:
Intellivix demonstrated Argos, a quadrupedal autonomous patrol robot, at the 2026 Smart Construction, Safety and AI Expo, the company announced on Nov. 25, 2026. The demonstration took place at the LH booth at KINTEX in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province, during the expo's Nov. 25 to 27 run.

Argos pairs AI video analytics with a quadrupedal robot and patrols construction sites on its own along designated routes. It analyzes surrounding video footage to detect collapsed workers, workers without safety helmets, entry into hazardous areas, and fire and smoke in real time. The robot covers blind spots that fixed CCTV cannot monitor. An in-house vision-language model and AI agents analyze hazards, and the system connects to the Gen AMS integrated AI safety monitoring platform to alert managers to incidents and hazards and to support patrol reporting.

"The key to construction site safety management is identifying hazards quickly and responding to them," an Intellivix official said. The official added: "To support hazard detection and on-site response, Argos's autonomous patrol and situational analysis capabilities will be combined with the AI video analytics technology deployed at LH construction sites."

LH operates the Real-time Integrated Construction Information System (RICS) and uses Neulbom A-Eye at high-risk sites. Intellivix has previously supplied AI video analytics to LH.

KT Cloud announced on Nov. 26 that it will build a 110MW AI data center cluster in Ansan, Gyeonggi Province. The Singapore-based asset manager Keppel is KT Cloud's partner in what is described as Keppel's first data center project in South Korea.

The cluster consists of a 60MW Ansan 2 AIDC and a 50MW Ansan 1 AIDC that is already under construction, and KT Cloud plans to integrate the operations of the two. The facility has a gross floor area of 52,622 square meters, or about 15,918 pyeong, with two underground floors and eight aboveground floors. Construction begins this month, and operations are scheduled to start in 2030. The site is about 2.5 kilometers from Ansan 1 AIDC, and liquid cooling infrastructure will be installed on all floors.

The project is part of KT Group's strategy to expand AIDC capacity to more than 1 gigawatt by 2031. The group also has plans for locations in Gunsan and Cheongna.

stories.Summary:
Samsung SDS announced ten executive promotions on Nov. 24, 2026. Four executive vice presidents and six vice presidents were promoted. Three of the four new executive vice presidents came from the Strategic Marketing Office, which accounted for four promotions in total. The Cloud Services Division accounted for three promotions.

Together the two units produced 70% of the promotions. The AX Center, the Solutions Division and the Logistics Division each had one promotion. The new executive vice presidents include Moon Kwan-hwi, head of the Distribution and Services Account Management Team; Lee Je-na, head of the Product Strategy Team; Lee Ji-hwan, head of the Financial Consulting Team; and Han Sang-won, head of the Managed Service Provider Business Team, who was promoted from the Cloud Services Division. All three Cloud Services promotions came from managed service provider organizations, which cover cloud migration, deployment and operations. Three of the promoted executives are women.

stories.Headline: Krafton releases Raon-1 mini AI model with in-house architecture and open license
stories.Summary:
Krafton released the full version of Raon-1 mini, its in-house large language model, on Nov. 25. The model was developed entirely in-house, from architecture to training. It uses a mixture-of-experts architecture that activates 4 billion of its 30 billion parameters. Krafton says proprietary linear attention technology improves response speed and reduces inference costs.

The full version improves on the preview in reasoning and complex task execution, according to the company. It scored 64.9 on the MultiChallenge benchmark, which measures instruction-following across turns, up 5.9 points from the preview. Krafton said the model "outperformed all six comparable overseas models." It scored 72.3 on GDPval and 55.9 on BrowseComp Plus, benchmarks that evaluate agent task execution, the highest scores among comparable mixture-of-experts models, the company said.

The model adds adjustable reasoning with six selectable levels. Simple questions are answered without reasoning, while complex tasks get more computational resources. It was released on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license, free to download for research and commercial development, with a testing environment and API provided.

Krafton launched the Raon brand in April, following earlier open-source speech and vision models. The company plans a larger Raon-1 model and a real-time bidirectional speech model.

stories.Headline: Qinxuan Wang and co-authors propose VC-OPD, which trains small multimodal models using question-conditioned visual cues
stories.Summary:
A paper posted on November 27, 2026 proposes VC-OPD, or Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation, a method for training small Multimodal Large Language Models. The first author is Qinxuan Wang, and the co-authors are Zheyu Zhang, Yijing Yang, Han Shu, Chuang Wang, Peipei Yang, Shuo Tang, Jie Hu and Shiming Xiang. The work is listed under arXiv identifier 2611.32292. Earlier visual on-policy distillation gave the teacher cropped or zoomed image regions as privileged information, aimed at fine-grained perception.

The authors say such local pixel cues are not enough for complex visual reasoning, which needs global structure, spatial relationships and high-level semantics. VC-OPD instead extends the privileged information to question-conditioned visual cues, generated by advanced MLLMs, that capture key visual details, structural relationships and semantic evidence for each question. A multi-stage quality filtering step selects reliable cues. The cues are given only to the teacher during training, which the authors say enables token-level supervision along student trajectories.

The student learns to reason from the original image, so no extra information is needed at inference time. According to the authors, the method is made compatible with both open-weight and proprietary black-box models because the advanced MLLMs are used only to generate cues, and the paper states that experiments on STEM and general visual reasoning benchmarks showed consistent improvements across model scales, beating reinforcement learning and on-policy distillation baselines. A 4B-parameter model trained with VC-OPD outperformed many baselines of 8B parameters or more. The authors present this as a demonstration of capability transfer through question-conditioned cues.

Articles.Title: VC-OPD: Learning to See What Matters via Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation

stories.Headline: Researchers present FORGE, a forward-only framework that trains embedded neural networks inside black-box simulators
stories.Summary:
Ruiqi Shu, Tianrun Gao, Haomin Wen and Xiaomeng Huang introduced an online training framework called FORGE in an arXiv preprint dated 27 November 2026, posted on the arXiv preprint server under identifier 2611.31964. FORGE stands for Forward-Only Response and Gauss-Newton Estimation. It trains embedded networks using forward runs only, decoupling network derivatives from black-box simulator dynamics. It targets Fortran and C/C++ simulators with forward-only interfaces, where the standard alternative is solver backpropagation through time.

Stage I of FORGE uses a low-dimensional Gauss-Newton step that follows output-orthonormal weight directions and applies a final-layer correction against feature drift. Stage II perturbs spatial output fields, fits a gain-bounded causal linear response operator, and, via network backpropagation, updates all weights and solves for regularized target outputs.

The authors tested FORGE on five benchmarks in 2D and 3D covering phase separation, reaction-diffusion, fluid and MHD turbulence, and ocean circulation. On 2D coarse-solver tests the framework cut mean squared error by 50% to 96%, and on 3D coarse-solver tests by 70%. It performed 16% to 69% better than the strongest forward-only baseline and recovered 88% to 98% of the gains from solver backpropagation through time. Code was released at a URL.

stories.Headline: New book warns leadership crisis grows as AI changes offices
stories.Summary:
Christian Anschuetz and Luis Serpa are the co-authors of a new book, "True Titans: Leading Inside to Win Outside," which examines a leadership crisis. The authors say AI is changing how companies work. They argue the bigger issue is how leaders treat their staff, and that employees are worried about AI's effect on their future.

The authors say many corporate environments are built around fear. "One of the most prevailing emotions ... is fear," Anschuetz said. According to the authors, that fear grows as firms spend on technology while underinvesting in the people who use it. Serpa asked, "How are they going to be encouraged to challenge a machine?" Anschuetz said, "you better bring the people along with that technology."

The authors call the cycle the "Groundhog Loop," in which firms promise change but little changes for employees. They say breaking it starts with leaders changing themselves, and they urge holding leaders accountable and building an environment where employees can speak up without fear. "There's not enough transparency," Anschuetz said. The authors say change need not start with a major overhaul, and they tell leaders to show change rather than talk about it.

The book is sold through major book retailers and at TrueTitans.com. The article was by Cassidie Stevens of FOX45 News, reported from Baltimore by WBFF, and published Thursday, November 26, 2026 at 9:20 PM.

stories.Headline: AI Assurance Council launches certification for project managers in applied AI use
stories.Summary:
The AI Assurance Council has launched a certification for project managers, which it calls the first applied AI credential for a specific job role. Enrolment is now open. The certification is aimed at project and program managers, as well as PMO and delivery leads, Scrum masters and agile leads.

The exam assesses how candidates use AI in routine project work, not their ability to manage AI projects. It focuses on planning, reporting, risk logs and stakeholder communication, with questions based on project scenarios involving AI-produced work in which candidates judge trust, checking and escalation. The pass mark is 70 per cent, with verification and quality control weighted at 30 per cent and applied workflow at 25 per cent. The remaining areas cover AI limits, risk, ethics, compliance and judgement. The exam is taken online under proctored conditions, machine-marked against a fixed answer key, and reviewed by a named staff member who checks the recording and script. Results are issued within three working days.

Danny Heng, Executive Director of the AI Assurance Council, said: "Project managers were among the first to put AI to work, writing status reports, summarising meetings and drafting plans." He added: "nobody can currently tell which of them are doing it well." He also said: "An AI-generated status report can look perfect and still be wrong." Durga Rajesh R, Director of Assurance and Technology at the council, said: "Most AI courses for project managers teach prompts." He added: "We weighted this examination the other way." He also said: "The largest share of marks goes to verification, because that is where AI use on a project succeeds or fails."

The credential is valid for two years and has no formal prerequisites, though the council recommends experience running or coordinating projects. It builds on the entry-level Certified Applied AI Associate, which the council says has been taken by candidates in 40 countries. Holders appear on a public register, and employers can verify results online. The council says the credential is intended to sit alongside PMP rather than replace it, as evidence of applied AI competence plus existing experience.

AI subscription sales rose 20% to 100 million yuan, about 16% of learning segment revenue.

Shares fell nearly 8% over four trading days but are up 77% since January. Cash flow for the first nine months was 152.1 million yuan, compared with an outflow of 129 million yuan a year earlier, while the third quarter had a cash outflow of 30 million yuan. First-nine-month learning revenue grew 6.7% and smart devices fell 39%, and new advertising revenue sources were up 50% year-over-year for three quarters. Youdao Dictionary has more than 1 billion users globally, and the company's P/E ratio is 69, versus Duolingo at 49, Kingsoft at 31, New Oriental at 15 and TAL at 7.7.

CEO Zhou Feng leads the company, which calls itself an AI solutions provider for learning and advertising. Six of seven Yahoo Finance analysts rate the stock a buy, and Huatai Securities maintained a buy rating. Independent analyst Su Youning said: "The market isn’t unwilling to value AI companies but it’s only willing to value companies where AI can be monetized."

NetEase founded Youdao in 2006, and Youdao Dictionary launched in 2007. The company introduced its Confucius large language model in 2023. A 2021 policy cost its online education business 41% of revenue, and AI agents from general-purpose models could undercut Youdao's LLM. stories.Headline: Researchers call for proactive AI tools to improve diabetes care
stories.Summary:
Rhiannon E. Hawkes and Lizheng Shi, researchers, have co-authored an editorial on digital health and artificial intelligence in diabetes care. The editorial, titled "Using digital diabetes care's promise in AI times," was published in BMC Digital Health in 2026 as volume 4, article 46. Diabetes affects more than one in ten adults worldwide, and worldwide economic losses are seen surpassing 2.1 trillion dollars by 2030. The condition means elevated blood glucose levels, and its complications include vision loss, nerve pain, amputation and cardiovascular problems. Traditional monitoring relies on finger-prick testing and manual records, which give isolated snapshots rather than continuous trends, and frequent testing is inconvenient and risks inaccurate readings.

Digital tools offer real-time data and remote communication, including continuous glucose monitors, smart insulin pens and mobile apps. Mobile health interventions improve glycaemic control and self-efficacy, with the benefit strongest when clinician feedback or decision-support tools are included, and digital education programmes are acceptable and clinically effective. Patient disengagement remains a critical bottleneck, and the authors say research is needed on which tool components users engage with and on the volume and delivery mode of clinician support. Continuous glucose monitors give real-time readings and predictive alerts, but uptake is limited by inconsistent insurance reimbursement, with Medicaid coverage gaps in the United States and NHS funding restrictions for adults with type 2 diabetes in the United Kingdom cited. An Australian nationally subsidised programme proved cost-effective.

Other barriers include poor workflow alignment, inadequate broadband and patient reluctance to share data due to absent governance frameworks. The authors urge transparent, accessible and secure tools that serve users with limited digital literacy, and they foresee AI in wearable monitors and virtual chatbots. They describe a shift toward what they call "agentic digital health technologies, moving away from passive, rule-based systems toward proactive, intelligent platforms capable of autonomous reasoning, planning, and task execution." An upcoming journal collection in BMC Digital Health will follow.

stories.Headline: Harvard and MIT researchers find RNA counts per cell limit single-cell AI model learning
stories.Summary:
A study published Thursday in Nature Machine Intelligence finds that the learning of single-cell models rises logarithmically with the number of RNA molecules counted per cell. The work was led by Allon Klein, a systems biologist at Harvard Medical School, and Gokul Gowri, a Tayebati Postdoctoral Fellow at MIT. It suggests that for some tasks, measurement quality rather than cell count limits what models can learn. The paper appeared in the journal on Thursday.

The study expresses performance as the information a model retains about a cell, measured in bits. It treats the signal-to-noise ratio as proportional to unique molecular identifiers per cell, which label every RNA molecule before PCR amplification. Model capacity is defined as the most information extractable from a noiseless measurement, and noise sensitivity as the signal-to-noise level at which better measurement adds at most half a bit. A lower noise sensitivity means a model tolerates more noise.

At fewer than 1,000 UMIs per cell, Geneformer, a transformer pretrained on about 30 million single-cell transcriptomes and described in Nature in 2023, came within half a bit of its ceiling, the authors report. Its ceiling was 0.4 to 1.4 bits below that of scVI, a variational autoencoder, according to the paper, whose supplement gives the gap as 0.6 to 1.1 bits. scVI was noise-sensitive at about 4,000 UMIs per cell on a protein-abundance task. A company release claims the study covers more than 2,000 model-task-noise combinations, while the arXiv version reports 1,670 fitted models across three data types.

Dan Raviv, director of computational biology and machine learning at Cellular Intelligence, is among the authors, and the arXiv author list gives company affiliations for Igor Sadalski, Dan Raviv and Jonathan Rosenfeld. Klein is a scientific co-founder of Cellular Intelligence, which was founded in 2023, was formerly known as Somite.ai and has raised more than $70 million. Micha Breakstone, the company's CEO, said: "drug discovery has long relied on trial and error because researchers cannot reliably predict how cells respond to therapeutics". The company says it plans to license models to pharmaceutical partners and is building a universal foundation model of cell signaling.

The paper notes that mRNA detection probability is well below 50% for many technologies, and that one droplet platform detects about 10% of mRNA while reaching up to 65% cell recovery.

stories.Headline: Researchers propose SympNO, a symplectic neural operator that learns Hamiltonian PDE flow maps
stories.Summary:
A paper posted on Zenodo on November 27, 2026 proposes an intrinsically structure-preserving symplectic neural operator that learns the flow maps of Hamiltonian partial differential equations. The architecture is called SympNO, and the work extends the construction behind G-SympNet into an operator setting. Conventional symplectic networks such as G-SympNet preserve symplecticity by composing maps that update either the coordinate or the momentum using the gradient of a scalar potential, but they were designed for finite-dimensional Hamiltonian ordinary differential equations and perform poorly on spatial discretizations. SympNO replaces the finite-dimensional gradient module with a functional gradient module in the style of a Fourier neural operator.

The paper proves that SympNO approximates fixed-time flow maps, reaching arbitrary accuracy under certain assumptions. Numerical experiments were run on Hamiltonian PDEs including the wave equation, the Klein-Gordon equation and the Schrödinger equation. According to the paper, SympNO outperforms G-SympNet, FNO and SNO, with better one-step and long-time prediction accuracy. The work carries DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24560672.

HackenProof, a crypto bug bounty platform, began using AI in October 2026 to sort 70% of its submissions without human help. The platform aims to reach 85% by the end of 2026. In the third quarter, it handled about 6,100 bug reports a month, which is 2.4 times the volume of December 2025.

Rival platform Immunefi reported a 136% year-over-year rise in submissions in the first nine months of 2026. Last week it introduced a tool that flags duplicates before they are submitted. Bug bounty programs pay researchers for finding security flaws. AI finds real vulnerabilities but also swells the number of invalid reports.

Dmitry Tokarev, founder of crypto wallet provider Bron, described the situation as "bringing a sword to a gunfight." February was identified as a turning point, when Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 handled larger codebases and longer tasks. HackerOne saw a shift away from human-only submissions. In October 2026, Firedancer, a Solana validator client by Jump Crypto, began burning 1 SOL per bug report, with no refund even for duplicates.

Tony Lee, vice president of operations at HackerOne, said the change would last "for the foreseeable future." In a November update published Tuesday, HackerOne said it required researcher identity verification in the third quarter, expanded its triage team and used AI agents, and in October gave customers control over report volume. Its report volume rose 22% in the third quarter.

Insurer QBE and consultancy Control Risks said on Wednesday that they forecast more disruptive cyber incidents in 2027, citing the "industrialization of AI" as a factor across 14 markets studied. Mike Blank, chief product officer at R3, expects hacks to rise sharply in 2027. "The real difference will be between protocols where a stolen key can drain everything and those where it can only pause operations," he said.

Through natural-language conversations, travelers and corporate travel managers will be able to search, compare and book flights and hotels, and manage existing itineraries and post-booking services.

Sabre has introduced its Mosaic Travel Connector in beta. The connector works across major large language models and links AI interfaces to Sabre's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, which lets AI assistants reach travel inventory and booking functions. More than 80 partners are in pilot or production with the technology. Sabre introduced its initial agentic APIs and MCP server in 2025.

The event-driven APIs monitor travel arrangements continuously, tracking airline and hotel prices against thresholds and alerting travelers and agencies when fares or rates fall. Booking-window intelligence identifies advantageous purchasing moments. The APIs also identify passengers affected by flight delays and cancellations and transmit alerts to connected systems immediately, so a human advisor, AI assistant or autonomous agent can respond.

Sabre says more than 99% of its computing infrastructure runs on cloud, handling over one billion travel shopping requests daily and approximately 50 petabytes of travel data. The company sees agentic commerce as a new distribution channel. It plans to extend the connector across more AI platforms in 2027.

PDF Spaces enables cross-document workflows across sources.

The Edit PDF tool modifies text, fonts and layout directly, and it can replace, move, resize or delete images. The scope of editing depends on fonts, password protection and layout. The AI Assistant can compare two documents and analyze charts and tables, and it handles seven languages. PDF Spaces consolidates PDFs, links and text into one workspace. The full AI features require a paid plan or add-on, while the free version limits the number of AI Assistant requests and offers more than 25 online conversion tools on a free account.

stories.Headline: Rebellion Research explains how AI scores rank international stocks for potential outperformance
stories.Summary:
An article published by Rebellion Research explains how AI scores rank international stocks that may outperform. It covers the signals that strengthen or weaken an assessment and the valuation discounts used in the analysis. The article notes that international stocks beat US stocks by about 14 percentage points last year, but says that recent gap alone is not evidence of durable alpha. The AI score is a ranking signal, not a calibrated probability, according to the article.

In tests on US All Cap stocks from 2015 to 2025, 61% to 65% of months showed positive active returns, a result the article says is not a forecast for international markets. Cross-border comparisons are complex because of differences in accounting, liquidity, politics and valuation norms, and the article says model output needs interpretation alongside country, sector and currency risks. A high score or a low multiple is not a forecast. The article names several fund holdings as of April 30, 2026: Fidelity International Value Fund held 3.8% in Banco Santander, Fidelity Diversified International Fund held 2.4% in Rheinmetall, and Fidelity China Region Fund held 23.2% in Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing.

European financial stocks made up 23% of a portfolio as of that date, which the article says shows sector exposure rather than proof of undervaluation. The article says passive global index funds track a defined benchmark, while AI strategies select or weight securities by model scores. Currency movements affect returns in an investor's base currency, and hedging reduces currency sensitivity but changes the risk drivers. Emerging markets carry heightened foreign-currency, liquidity, regulatory, political and economic risks, and feature quality depends on the dating and comparability of observations.

Benchmark choice affects the conclusion, and a valuation discount may reflect overlooked growth or weaker earnings quality. Tax treatment depends on investor circumstances and jurisdictions, and data privacy and regulatory rules vary across jurisdictions; backtests must avoid look-ahead and survivorship bias, and transaction arrangements, currency conversion and market access determine the costs of foreign stocks. Model limitations include incomplete data, changing relationships and concentrated exposures. Alternative data includes retail prices, job postings, shipping activity and news coverage, and the data pipeline should map companies to consistent identifiers, with timestamping mattering for alternative inputs.

The agentic offensive framework was used by groups including Salt Typhoon, Crystal Typhoon, and the North Korean groups Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Other involved actors include the China-state-aligned Storm-0940 and the Cambodia-based Storm-3358.

The tool automates credential attacks as well as reconnaissance and exploitation. It targets financial institutions, cloud environments, and the IT software ConnectWise. Victims include the European Commission, the UK registrar 123 Reg, and targets in India and South Korea. According to the Register, 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants were targeted, with privileged access reached in as little as minutes or three hours.

The Microsoft threat intelligence team stated, "These campaigns illustrate how threat actors use ARTEX to automate various stages of the attack chain." The framework was released publicly in July 2026, but the original repository was deleted in October 2026. In November 2026, the Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of the tool. The Register reports that a GitHub user named "Autumn-27" is linked to the tool, and 130 variants of ARTEX exist, including Infrawatch.

The Register notes that the framework does not use new attack techniques but instead chains known attacks at machine speed. AWS described the theft of AI credentials as "industrial scale." The FBI and AWS issued warnings regarding these activities earlier in November 2026.

stories.Headline: Ashoka professors explain how AI proves theorems using Lean and reinforcement learning
stories.Summary:
Aalok Thakkar, Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Ashoka University, and Subhashis Banerjee, Professor of Computer Science at Ashoka University, explained how AI proves theorems by combining large language models with Lean proof assistants, with reinforcement learning refining proofs and automated verification checking every logical step. In September, OpenAI announced a fluid proof describing a fluid at rest with smooth force and infinite speed, which settles the Navier, Stokes equations, a Millennium Prize Problem open since 1934. In October, OpenAI and Anthropic released algorithms that decide propositional satisfiability sub-exponentially, and more than 800 papers rest on the Exponential Time Hypothesis, which those algorithms refute; a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a Millennium Prize Problem open since 1859, was announced last week by Levent Alpöge of Anthropic, found with Claude. Each proof was checked using the Lean proof assistant, and human review of all three proofs is in progress. Large language models are functions with billions of parameters, and pre-training reads tens of trillions of tokens from the internet, books, code and papers.

The model is not taught grammar, facts or logic, and a fluent proof can hide a fatal gap, because it is trained to be coherent, not correct. Lean 4 is a programming language for step-by-step proofs, and its kernel accepts a proof only if every step follows logic. Mathlib holds nearly 300,000 theorems, built by over 700 contributors. Lean is not AI, with no learning and no probabilities, but it checks candidate proofs by the million and says where and why a proof fails, though it certifies only the statement as written. The Riemann Hypothesis statement takes a few lines, while its proof runs to 17 million lines.

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has the model attempt a problem many times while Lean marks success or failure, with the reward coming from the checker, not a person, since sound reasoning succeeds more often than not. The loop of the model generating, Lean checking and verdicts improving the model follows. Thakkar and Banerjee said: "The AI proposes, Lean judges, and humans supply the statements and the judgement of what matters." Verification is not understanding, mathematicians say the Navier, Stokes proof taught them little, and trial and error makes AI as good as its checker, while weak checkers let AI please the checker without doing the task.

stories.Headline: India's Defence Space Agency invites startups to build AI and anti-jamming systems for orbit
stories.Summary:
The Defence Space Agency is seeking Indian research institutions and startups to develop space-based cyber defence, AI-driven orbital analytics and anti-jamming systems. Air Vice Marshal Manu Midha, Director General of the agency, announced the push on Thursday, November 26, 2026, at Tec-Verse 2026 in Chennai. He said space is now a contested military theatre. "If an adversary blinds, jams or disrupts our orbital architecture, our terrestrial forces risk losing their eyes, ears and nervous system," he said.

The agency has identified three areas for the research ecosystem to contribute to. The first covers high-performance computing, quantum technologies and edge AI, including sovereign AI and radiation-hardened edge computing onboard, along with quantum-resistant cryptography and quantum key distribution. The second covers electronic warfare and resilient satellite systems, including anti-jamming payloads, resilient transponders and space situational awareness sensors. The third covers indigenous components to cut reliance on foreign supply chains, with priority on specialised electronic materials, power amplifiers, thermal protection, chipsets and microprocessors. Midha also called for indigenous radar and electro-optical sensor networks for debris tracking and for detecting adversarial proximity operations in orbit. "Do not build technology in isolation and do not wait for the traditional tender to come," he said.

Lt. Gen. Praveen Bakshi, Commandant of the Military College of Telecommunication Engineering, said the armed forces need secure and reliable communication networks, and want military data held in private clouds for cybersecurity. He said mobile forces need connectivity at the tactical edge and called for software-defined radios with indigenous waveforms and AI applications that give real-time awareness of enemy positions. The forces are engaging with the Defence Research and Development Organisation and the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, and are associated with the national AI, semiconductor and quantum missions.

At one point the index looked headed toward a 5% selloff, and the furious rally that followed was the greatest intraday rebound since April 2025. Much of Wednesday's losses were accounted for by tech stocks, and by the Thanksgiving holiday logoff, the benchmark was down 0.6%. "This is bigger than Jensen Huang being removed.

This is skepticism that had been creeping into markets well before that," he said. Zidle also said credit investors were growing anxious: "Credit investors, who are really the lifeblood of this AI trade, are getting very nervous here." Investment-grade yield premiums barely budged on Monday and sat near their highest level since May 2025, while yield premiums for Oracle and SpaceX kept climbing. stories.Headline: Job-loss insurance add-ons in India pay loan instalments for eligible salaried staff after layoffs
stories.Summary:
Tech job losses worldwide reached 2,09,841 through November 2026, according to figures tracking 742 layoff events compiled by TrueUp. That works out to 642 tech jobs cut per day in 2026, up from 579 per day in 2025. The figures cover all tech job cuts, not only those linked to AI. Job-loss insurance is sold in India as a policy add-on, Paisabazaar says, attached to home, accident or critical illness cover. It can pay out toward loan instalments and other financial commitments, with support of up to three months while a person looks for work.

Salaried employees of registered companies are generally eligible under Paisabazaar's terms, while self-employed workers, casual, seasonal, temporary and contractual workers are excluded. Buying the add-on does not guarantee a claim payout. Some plans cover job loss caused by critical illness or disability, and termination or temporary suspension may qualify under the terms. Whether an AI-caused termination is covered depends on the policy wording, and companies rarely cite AI as a direct reason for layoffs. Policies carry a waiting period of 30 to 90 days after the policy starts, and job loss during that period may rule out a payout.

Job loss during probation is excluded, as are voluntary resignation and retirement, and dismissal for poor performance, dishonesty or fraud is ineligible. A policyholder should read the job-loss clause before buying and compare the policy conditions with the employer's termination letter. To claim, the policyholder should inform the insurer in writing and send proof of unemployment, along with a signed claim form and the employer's termination letter. The last three months' salary slips and Form 16 should be kept, as should the employer's contact details, the policy copy, and ID and age proof. The insurer reviews the documents before deciding on a payout, and some policies make regular payments after an eligible job loss.

stories.Headline: Japan aims to become a leading AI nation to reduce reliance on other countries
stories.Summary:
The government of Japan announced its goal to be a leading AI nation on November 25, 2026. This objective follows similar efforts by China and the United States.

The plan involves revising three national security documents in late 2026. These updates will outline economic security sections and include investments in automated driving and physical AI. The government will also conduct risk assessments for four categories of strategic goods, which include medical, food, and energy goods.

The Liberal Democratic Party of Japan aims to reduce the country's reliance on other nations for AI. The party intends to increase state support for stable supplies and strengthen supply chains with partners it considers reliable.

According to japantimes.co.jp, these moves come as diplomacy and defense depend on technology. The government seeks to advance its Free and Open Indo-Pacific vision and oppose economic coercion, including export restrictions from China.

stories.Headline: AI conflict drives Chinese government bond yields to record low
stories.Summary:
Investors shifted toward defensive assets during November 2026 because of volatility surrounding artificial intelligence trades. This widespread risk aversion drove the yield on benchmark longer-dated Chinese government bonds to a record low. Market participants reacted to the turmoil by increasing their purchases of sovereign debt and dividend stocks. These actions indicate a cautious approach to buying as traders sought safety from the unstable AI market. The yield on the 10-year sovereign debt of China fell to a historic low of 1.565 per cent during this month.

At the same time, the Shanghai Stock Exchange Dividend Index grew by approximately 7 per cent from the beginning of the year. This specific index showed a strong performance that surpassed most other primary gauges used to track Chinese equities. These shifts reflect a broader movement toward assets that provide more stability during periods of high market volatility. Zhang Shidong reported from Shanghai that investors are currently hunkering down in defensive positions to protect their capital.

He noted that the instability of the artificial intelligence trade has sparked a general desire to avoid risk. This environment has led traders to load up on dividend stocks while simultaneously driving down government bond yields. The reporter suggests that these movements are a direct result of the current strife within the AI sector. More to follow.

stories.Headline: UBS predicts Chinese AI chip shipments will grow nearly sixfold by 2030
stories.Summary:
Annual shipments of domestic artificial intelligence accelerators in China are expected to increase nearly sixfold between 2025 and 2030. According to a research note from UBS, these shipments will likely exceed 10 million units by the end of that period. This growth occurs as the government in Beijing emphasizes technological self-reliance following increased scrutiny of chip exports from the United States. The report identifies Cambricon Technologies and Biren Technology as the front runners in this expanding domestic market. The projected growth requires shipments of locally made processors to rise from 1.7 million units in 2025.

This increase would allow Chinese suppliers to capture 83 per cent of their home market by 2027. By 2028, the share of the domestic market held by these local suppliers is expected to reach 88 per cent. Such a shift in market share follows recent challenges faced by the American company Nvidia. Jimmy Yu, who serves as the head of China technology at UBS Securities, provided these projections in a note published on Tuesday.

He suggests that the ability to secure key components and manufacturing capacity will be the primary competitive edge for chipmakers. This advantage will be most critical over the next one to two years of development. The analysis links these trends to the broader geopolitical tensions regarding the export of high-end technology. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Police lieutenant Seo Hae-won wins top public safety invention award for AI injury-measuring sticker
stories.Summary:
At an awards ceremony on Thursday at the National Assembly in Seoul, the winners of the 2026 Public Safety Invention Challenge were announced by the Ministry of Intellectual Property. Lieutenant Seo Hae-won of Ulsan Jungbu Police Station won the National Assembly Speaker's Award. Seo's sticker helps artificial intelligence measure injuries in photographs. The same bruise can look different depending on camera angle and distance.

The sticker is placed beside an injury before it is photographed, and the AI uses the sticker's scale to measure the size of the injury. The tool is intended for domestic violence, child abuse and elder abuse cases. Thirty winners were selected from 868 entries. Judges weighed originality, field use and commercial potential, and the contest is in its ninth year.

The contest was co-hosted by the Korea Customs Service, the Korean National Police Agency, the National Fire Agency, the Korea Forest Service, the Korea Coast Guard and Reps. Jang Chul-min and Jeon Eun-su. Park Hee-young of Incheon Airport Customs received a gold award from the interior and safety minister for a "chair of truth" that screens for concealed drugs using pressure and temperature readings. Song Se-min of the Korea Forest Service received a gold award from the intellectual property minister for a chainsaw system that detects RFID tags on workwear and stops the saw within a set distance of the tags.

Following consultations with experts, patent applications for the winning designs had been filed, the Ministry of Intellectual Property said, and the agencies will help the inventors secure patents and transfer their technology.

Articles.Title: AI bruise-measuring tool wins top prize at public safety contest

stories.Headline: Raleigh tenant faces eviction after apartment AI assistant approves later rent date
stories.Summary:
Laura Mack, a tenant at Colony Townhome Apartments in Raleigh, North Carolina, was evicted after an email exchange that appeared to approve a later rent payment date. The exchange began on 8 November, when Mack asked when she could settle her $3,934.17 overdue rent balance. The reply appeared to approve a payment on 30 November, stating: "Paying on November 30, the last day of the month, works." Mack received an eviction notice on 16 November and was evicted on 19 November, 11 days before the payment date.

The emails reportedly showed no involvement by Olivia, the apartment complex's AI assistant. A leasing employee allegedly blamed Olivia for the messages, though the property has not publicly confirmed that explanation. Residents said Olivia answered rent and maintenance questions, and Mack cited personal details and bathroom ceiling maintenance in her messages. It is unclear whether employees reviewed the exchange before the eviction and whether the emails formed an enforceable agreement.

Alfred Leach, a Colony spokesperson, commented on 20 November, saying owners were "gathering information" and expected an update the following week. The company has remained silent on whether Olivia had authority to approve extensions. Jim Burgin, a North Carolina state Senator, said: "I think notification is one thing, and I think liability is another." Burgin introduced a "Bot Bill" requiring AI disclosure, which has not advanced in the legislature; he intends to pursue it next legislative session.

A 2024 ruling by the British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal found Air Canada liable after its chatbot gave wrong bereavement fare information, though the Canadian ruling does not determine North Carolina law. By 21 November Mack was staying in a hotel, and she tried challenging the eviction at the Wake County courthouse. Mack acknowledged responsibility for the overdue rent. The emails were first examined by local broadcaster WRAL.

stories.Headline: Columnist Robert Fouser judges human translators beat chatbots on Kawabata but match them on Camus
stories.Summary:
Robert J. Fouser, a former associate professor of Korean language education at Seoul National University, published an opinion column on AI and literary translation in The Korea Herald on Nov. 27, 2026. Fouser is based in Washington. The column appeared in the context of Minumsa's World Literature Series, which launched in 1998 with Ovid's "Metamorphoses."

The series published its 500th volume in June 2026, and Minumsa's website lists 504 volumes. According to the column, it is the first single Korean publisher literary series to pass 500 volumes. More than 50 titles in the series have sold over 100,000 copies, with Hermann Hesse's "Demian" the bestseller at about 813,000 copies. Hesse is the most represented author in the series, and every hundredth volume is a work by a Korean author, with 15 other Korean works interspersed through the series.

Fouser compared AI translations with human translations of the opening lines of three works. For Yasunari Kawabata's "Snow Country," he set Edward Seidensticker's first sentence, "The train came out of the long tunnel into the snow country," against chatbot versions. One chatbot wrote, "Emerging from the long border tunnel, it was snow country," and another wrote, "Past the long tunnel at the border, it was snow country." Fouser noted that the original Japanese has no train, and he declared the human translator the clear winner on "Snow Country."

For Albert Camus's "The Stranger," Fouser compared Stuart Gilbert's 1946 translation, "Mother died today," and Matthew Ward's 1988 translation, "Maman died today," with a chatbot's "Today, Mama died." He judged that the chatbots did well with Camus. For Yi Sang's "Wings," he used Walter K. Lew and Youngju Ryu's translation, "Have you heard about 'the genius who ended up a stuffed specimen'?" The chatbots used "taxidermied" or "taxidermy specimen" for "bakje," and they cautioned that the wording might sound strange and clinical. Fouser observed that the chatbots acted more like mentors on "Wings."

Human translators have done all the series' translations to date. Fouser suggested that translators may evolve into "translation editors" as AI advances.

stories.Headline: Microsoft drops the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028
stories.Summary:
Microsoft is removing the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system. WSUS, introduced as Software Update Services in 2005, manages and distributes Microsoft product updates. The change affects enterprises that manage updates for many devices, but it has no impact on home users or on users of Microsoft Configuration Manager. WSUS was officially deprecated in September 2024, when Microsoft said it would keep the feature functioning.

Updates will continue to flow through the channel, and support continues for earlier Windows Server releases, with Windows Server 2025 supported through its lifecycle. Microsoft, via TechGig, "encourages businesses to adopt cloud-based solutions for keeping endpoints and servers up to date." For server update management, Azure Update Manager is recommended, and for client update management, Windows Autopatch and Microsoft Intune are recommended. The release was announced last week at the Ignite 2026 conference. Testing is available through the Windows Insider Program for Windows Server and through enrollment in the Windows Server Technology Adoption Program (TAP). The TechGig report was published on 28 November 2026.

stories.Headline: Korea TOEIC Committee adds glasses stickers and metal detectors to block AI cheating
stories.Summary:
The Korea TOEIC Committee under YBM announced six anti-cheating measures on 26 November 2026, to take effect with the regular test on 29 November 2026. All test-takers' glasses will be inspected, and tamper-evident security stickers will be affixed to eyeglass frames. The stickers leave traces when removed, and their colors and sizes will vary each exam. Large-area stickers will also be applied to clothing buttons, and hats are prohibited.

Personal mechanical pencils are banned, with up to two pencils allowed on the desk. One eraser with its cover removed is allowed, along with ID meeting regulations. An analog wristwatch is allowed but must be set on the desk rather than worn, and spare erasers are barred from the desk. Other belongings must be bagged and stored in a designated place, and metal detector inspections will be conducted.

Restroom users, early leavers due to illness and suspected cheaters will be subject to inspection. The committee is pursuing radio-frequency detectors, with plans to deploy them at all test sites nationwide. Post-exam screening will be strengthened during score processing, and a cheating report center will be activated on the website. Online cheating-recruitment ads will be monitored constantly, and problematic ads will be reported to the Broadcast Media Communications Deliberation Commission. AI cheating has been uncovered in the certified tax accountant exam and the CSAT.

stories.Headline: Bank of Korea raises 2027 growth forecast to 4.1 percent on AI chip exports
stories.Summary:
The Bank of Korea raised its 2027 growth forecast to 4.1 percent on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026, in Seoul, citing strong AI-linked semiconductor exports that boosted momentum. The revision was 1.2 percentage points above the previous 2.9 percent forecast released in August. It was the third time the 2027 projection has been raised since February, when it stood at 1.8 percent. The bank said the figure is its highest new-year forecast since December 2009, when it projected 4.6 percent for 2010, and above its May 2021 forecast of 4 percent for 2022.

The Bank of Korea also raised its 2026 growth forecast to 3.9 percent from 3.3 percent, which it said would be the highest annual rate since 2021, when growth was 4.7 percent. It projected 2028 growth at 3 percent. Exports are forecast to rise 10.9 percent in 2026 and 8 percent in 2027, up from earlier forecasts of 9.7 percent and 4.6 percent. The bank said: "Despite downward pressures from renewed tensions in the Middle East and a stock market correction, faster-than-expected semiconductor performance stirred up growth in 2026."

Shin said inflation is expected to reach the 2 percent target in 2028. The bank said 2027 chip-led growth is seen spreading economy-wide, citing government expansionary fiscal policy and delayed U.S. semiconductor tariffs. Quarterly growth was 1.8 percent in the first quarter of 2026, the strongest since 2.2 percent in the third quarter of 2020, followed by 0.6 percent in the second quarter, above the bank's May forecast of 0.2 percent, and 1 percent in the third quarter, above its earlier 0.3 percent forecast. The International Monetary Fund projects 3.9 percent growth for 2026 and Moody's 3.7 percent.

stories.Headline: Posco signs 26 AI data center and materials MOUs at sustainable forum
stories.Summary:
Posco hosted its 2026 Sustainable Forum from Nov. 16 to 18 at Songdo ConvensiA in Incheon, drawing about 1,000 participants, including 450 representatives from partner companies. Posco said the theme was "The Path to AI and Green Transformation (AX & GX), Sustainable Materials Leading New Growth." The program featured a keynote by futurist Jonathan Brill, presentations from Google Cloud and UBTECH Robotics leaders, and 31 sessions. At the forum, Posco signed more than 26 memorandums of understanding with partners covering AI data centers, shipbuilding and low-carbon materials. The company also highlighted its Early Vendor Involvement model, which brings steel specifications into the initial design stage.

On Nov. 11, 2026, Posco signed an AI data center MOU with GS Group under which Posco will supply specialized materials and solutions while GS Group oversees infrastructure development and operations, handling planning, power, engineering and liquid cooling. PosMAC coating is applied to data centers and power infrastructure. Posco plans to expand production and sales of POCEL, a battery-case material, with global EV battery demand projected at about 3 TWh by 2030, as it builds an integrated materials ecosystem for the AI era, Lee So-youn of Korea JoongAng Daily reported. Separately, EVE Energy unveiled an AI data center energy storage portfolio at RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, part of North America's Smart Energy Week, in an announcement dated Nov. 26, 2026.

The portfolio spans source-grid, distribution and cabinet layers. The 1P 5MWh ESS system offers 5 MWh of capacity in a 20-foot container, a peak rate of up to 1.2P, 20,000 equivalent cycles in frequency regulation and 93.6 percent system efficiency. According to EVE, auxiliary power is cut 20 percent, and at 100 MWh scale the system uses three fewer cabinets, cuts transport costs over 40 percent and reduces land use over 13 percent, with 99 percent annual system availability. Its frequency-regulation cell has 315 Ah capacity and 395 Wh/L volumetric energy density.

The Mr.Giant 3.0 long-duration storage system offers over 95.5 percent efficiency after 700 days and 10,000 cycles. The Fortron 6C/10C backup power cabinet delivers 660 kW for five minutes and has a 15-year design life. A rack-level system combines BBU and CBU, with BBU discharge rates up to 48C, backup power transfer under 2 milliseconds and supercapacitor response of 1 millisecond or less. EVE said it ranked No. 2 in storage cell shipments in the first half of 2026, with 230 GWh in cumulative global shipments, and that it is on the S&P Global Tier 1 integrator list.

stories.Headline: Korean sociology journal rejects paper over AI ethics breach as sanctions rise
stories.Summary:
In September, the Korean Association for Critical Sociology’s journal Economy and Society flagged a submitted paper before publication for an AI-related ethics violation, the first such case at that journal. The references in the paper differed from the originals. The author said AI had been used in part, but that the topic had been written directly and the references checked. The society rejected that explanation and imposed sanctions.

The cases come as AI use in papers spreads and submissions rise, with sanctions and retractions accumulating and credibility concerns growing while countermeasures lag. In August last year, the Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs caught a paper citing literature that did not exist; the institute said the case “went beyond simple carelessness or errors arising from AI.” This August, the Cultural Territory Research Institute retracted a paper that cited false information recommended by AI. In May, the editorial board of East and West Studies retracted an AI-generated fake paper on China’s space industry.

References underpin credibility and citations are used for measurement, but compiling them takes much time and effort, and some researchers delegate the work to AI and skip verification. Lee Geon-hyeok, a professor in the Department of Media and Communication at Changwon National University and president of the Korean Society for Journalism and Information Studies, said submissions “have increased exponentially to a level editorial boards can hardly handle.” He said that “In the past, we reviewed on the premise that references were properly cited, but now the situation is different,” and that the same phenomenon appears in doctoral exams, where a cited document did not exist. An unnamed national university research team said wrong information is now often partly wrong and that reviewers have little time to check meticulously. An unnamed professor at a private Seoul university heard of a colleague’s paper being superficially evaluated by AI.

There are also cases of AI use at the review stage. Last year, Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that researchers in Korea, the US and Japan, including at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology, hid invisible commands asking AI to rate papers highly. Caught researchers denied violations and attacked others’ papers, according to the report. An unnamed national university professor said AI is used to find hallucinated references and file reports, with anonymous tip-offs targeting specific individuals and targeted researchers filing counter-reports. Quantitative evaluation fuels AI overuse.

Some societies, including the Association for Critical Sociology, the Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs and the Cultural Territory Research Institute, created separate ethics rules saying AI is only an auxiliary tool and its use must be stated. Many organizations have no separate rules, including the Architectural Institute of Korea and the Korean Institute of Information Scientists and Engineers, which say rules are “currently preparing.” Joo Eun-seon, a professor in the Department of Social Welfare at Kyonggi University who helped create a journal AI guideline, said the key is disclosing transparently how much and what kind of AI help was used and that final research responsibility rests with humans. She said the time lag between AI use and ethics guidelines is far too great and that few universities have official guidelines.

Critics say quantity-over-quality evaluation fans AI use, with paper counts and citation counts weighing heavily in appointments and promotions. According to Jo Eun-ju, editor-in-chief of Economy and Society and a professor of sociology at Jeonbuk National University, it is time to question extreme quantitative evaluation practices, and researchers are pressured to publish many papers quickly. Ko Won-tae, a BK assistant professor in the College of Liberal Studies at Seoul National University, said low-quality papers mean a high cost to sift trustworthy knowledge. He said hallucinated citations may improve with AI advances, but that not reading cited papers could harm the research ecosystem.

stories.Headline: Trianz launches Concierto AI for in-perimeter enterprise AI use
stories.Summary:
Trianz, an enterprise transformation platform company, said on 26 November 2026 that its Concierto AI is now generally available worldwide. The platform runs AI inside the customer's own cloud or data center, so data, intellectual property and prompts stay within the customer's perimeter. It includes C/Composer, an AI assistant for knowledge workers, and C/Code, a coding agent for engineers. A kill-switch under customer control is also part of the offering.

Concierto AI is priced by users and workloads rather than by tokens, and unlimited usage is included in that pricing. Free trials begin on 26 November 2026 at concierto.ai. The platform's centerpiece is Sovereign Workforce Productivity, alongside services named Sovereign Transformations for the application estate, Sovereign Agentic AI for governed agents and Sovereign Operations for estate operations. It deploys on AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and on-premises.

Sri Manchala, CEO of Trianz, said: "Every technology shift opens a faultline, and companies either cross it or fall into it." The company points to more than 20 years of Trianz transformation expertise behind the release. Prashant Bhavaraju, VP and Global Head of Marketing at Trianz, was also named in the announcement.

The release was distributed by PRNewswire via Yonhap, which said it did not edit the press release content.
